articles.title: Fantasy Football: Hayden Winks' last-minute full-PPR draft strategy
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks offers up some strategy for those in full-PPR leagues.
articles.body:
It's time to directly address the 40% of leagues out there that play in full PPR. Today's column will go over my top 120 overall rankings, plus some strategy and top targets.

RB Jahmyr Gibbs: Given the chance, I'm choosing the No. 1 pick.

WR Puka Nacua: 23.8 PPR points per game were 3.4 more than the WR2 overall.

WR Ja'Marr Chase: WR1 on WR1 expected points in games with Joe Burrow healthy over the past 3 seasons.

RB Bijan Robinson: RB2 in receptions per game (4.6).

WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba: WR2 on WR5 usage last year on league-high 35% targets.

WR Amon-Ra St. Brown: 3-straight seasons with both 10+ TDs and 115+ receptions.

RB Christian McCaffrey: 24.0 PPR points per game last year were most in the NFL.

RB Jonathan Taylor: 24.8 PPR points per game through Week 13 with Daniel Jones.

WR CeeDee Lamb: WR9 on WR9 usage last year with George Pickens. Positive TD luck coming.

WR Justin Jefferson: Most PPR points per game (20.1) among WRs from 2022-2024 if we remove the Josh Dobbs and Jaren Hall games.

RB De'Von Achane: RB6 per game over past two seasons when MIA was 25th in points.

RB Kenneth Walker III: My LeSean-McCoy-with-Andy-Reid senses are tingling.

This is the position that takes the biggest hit going from half to full-PPR because … wait for it … they don't pile up receptions (points per reception, folks). While extremely simple, the reality is leagues don't factor this in enough. There should be a full round discount on all QBs here, and that includes Josh Allen up top.

Allen should not be drafted in the first four rounds of full PPR drafts.

The next crop of semi elite QBs shouldn't go until Round 6 at the earliest.

And this year's depth at QB goes well beyond the 12-team league starters. Kyler Murray, Jordan Love, Jared Goff, Jaxson Dart, Bo Nix and others are all legit low-end QB1 options who will be nearly free in drafts. The advice remains to double up in this tier and load up on a quality bench player at RB and WR before getting into the QB waters.

WR: Browns first-rounder KC Concepcion lit it up against SEC competition as a downfield and manufactured-touch threat. He was the best route runner in the class and has Jaylen Waddle-like explosiveness. He will be a great pro, and the Browns best weapon in no time. Coach Todd Monken said he's a Zay Flowers-type of player, and he just coached Flowers to a top-20 season. Concepcion will be better than Flowers long term, in my opinion. … Matthew Golden is taking on the Packers' Romeo Doubs role, one that turned in a WR37 finish on WR35 usage. Doubs wishes he had Golden's juice. The 4.2-speed first-rounder will be a full-time player, as the Packers truly only have three receivers to play this season. His tape was better than given credit for as a rookie, and he's been an MVP in camp. … Wan'Dale Robinson is going to do the same 'ol Wan'Dale thing. He's reunited with OC Brian Daboll, and the Titans' preseason offense looked very RPO heavy, which plays to his short-area strengths. He is the favorite over Carnell Tate for receptions. They just won't be pretty. They also weren't last year, when he was the PPR's WR17 on WR13 usage. … Makai Lemon is simply too great of a prospect to be nearly free in drafts. He'll overtake the inconsistent Dontayvion Wicks for 2-WR sets eventually, and when that happens, Lemon will be a FLEX play in a usually top-12 offense. … Jordan Addison had WR22 and WR26 per-game finishes as a rookie and sophomore, before J.J. McCarthy ruined the party. He's priced nowhere near that, and I think Kyler Murray is in the same tier as Sam Darnold and Kirk Cousins.

TE: Juwan Johnson will project best early on without first-round WR Jordyn Tyson, making him a great punt TE option or pairing with rehabbing stars, Tucker Kraft and George Kittle. Johnson was the TE5 in receptions and TE8 in yards per game after the Rashid Shaheed trade last year. … Terrance Ferguson is the mystery box on the Rams. Their lackluster WR depth and his second-round draft capital create an upside case worthy of a final-round pick. We'll see in Week 1. … Dalton Schultz was the TE16 on TE11 usage last year with Jayden Higgins, while the Texans were a very mediocre offense. He's a high-floor TE2.

articles.title: Plata de Lena Moreno en el prestigioso Grand Prix de Muju
articles.standfirst: Sólo la china Xing pudo con la española en la final de -67 kilos
articles.summary: Sólo la china Xing pudo con la española en la final de -67 kilos
articles.body: Lena Moreno Reyes, taekwondista alcarreña del Hankuk, ha logrado la medalla de plata en el Grand Prix de Muju (Corea del Sur), una de las competiciones más importantes del mundo del taekwondo. La española ha firmado una jornada apasionante, desplegando su mejor taekwondo y ganando cuatro combates con una gran autoridad y todos por un marcador de dos rondas a cero. En su debut, se enfrentó a la mexicana Leslie Soltero, quien fue campeona del mundo en 2022 y que venía de vencer en el Open de los Estados Unidos y en el de la República Dominicana. En octavos de final, la rival de la española sería la china Jie Song, segunda mejor taekwondista de su país y que presenta un palmarés excelso con medallas de oro en Grand Prix, Grand Slam, Campeonato de Asia y los Juegos Militares Mundiales; un combate extremadamente complejo que Lena dominó con mano de hierro. En cuartos de final, y a un paso de la medalla, Lena combatió con la representante rusa Anastasiia Bannova, considerada una de las mejores júniors del taekwondo de ese país. En semifinales se enfrentó a la croata Dora Mestrovic, taekwondista que presentaba un 2026 muy sólido ganando más del 80% de sus combates y mostrándose muy dominante en los torneos celebrados en Europa. Igualmente, Lena la venció por dos rondas a cero y se plantó en su primera final de Grand Prix, torneo de categoría G6, repartiendo muchos puntos al ranking internacional. Y en la final, la pupila de Jesús Ramal y Suvi Mikkonen se batió contra la china Jiani Xing en uno de los mejores combates de todo el fin de semana. Lena logró desplegar su estrategia encima del tapiz, manejando el centro del octógono y controlando los tiempos como ella quería en un primer momento. El enfrentamiento se fue al tercer y definitivo asalto y, con la victoria momentánea de la española, Xing logró remontar con varias acciones efectivas sobre la cabeza de la alcarreña. Este resultado es extraordinario para una Lena Moreno que ya fue medalla de bronce mundial el año pasado, en Wuxi (China) y que sigue con su progresión como una de las grandes perlas del taekwondo nacional. Debido a la categoría de la competición y al nivel mostrado sobre el tapiz, Lena Moreno encara la segunda mitad de la temporada con la expectativa de posicionarse bien en la lucha por acudir a los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028

NXT star Lexis King and former WWE colleague Carolina Cruz became engaged over the weekend.

"I always wondered what it would feel like to find the kind of love you see in the movies… and somehow, I got lucky enough to live it," she wrote on Instagram .

"You came into my life when I least expected it and became my best friend, my safe place, and the person I want beside me through every version of this life. Loving you has always felt easy, natural, and like something God had already written for me long before we ever met.

articles.title: Continúa el maleficio de 'Los Gallos' en casa: fuera de la final en Valencia
articles.standfirst: Tras acabar líderes del Gran Premio de España el sábado, fueron últimos en la única carrera de flota del domingo. Mantienen la segunda plaza en la general. Sólo Australia ha conseguido ganar en casa en las seis temporadas de competición
articles.summary: Tras acabar líderes del Gran Premio de España el sábado, fueron últimos en la única carrera de flota del domingo. Mantienen la segunda plaza en la general. Sólo Australia ha conseguido ganar en casa en las seis temporadas de competición
articles.body: A 'Los Gallos' se le sigue resistiendo el Gran Premio de España de SailGP. En las cuatro ediciones que se celebraron en Cádiz, nunca lograron entrar en la final. En Valencia todo apuntaba a que por fin se rompería el maleficio de los anfitriones. Acabaron líderes en la primera jornada tras firmar dos victorias y un segundo puesto. Este domingo, fueron últimos del Grupo B en la única carrera de flota -así llaman en la Fórmula 1 del mar a las regatas- que pudo celebrarse ante la falta de viento y la programación de las televisiones. Estaban previstas dos. Sólo los dos primeros de cada grupo pasaban a la final y al equipo de Botín acabó tercero con 14 puntos, empatado con Dinamarca que le 'birló' la segunda plaza porque en caso de empate se mira la última carrera, con la mala suerte de que fue la única que no ganó ayer España y sí Dinamarca. "Duele mucho, pero hay que usar este dolor para seguir para adelante y aprender. Estoy seguro de que nos va a ayudar e impulsar", reconoció Diego Botín, el piloto del equipo, en la zona mixta. Su cara, al igual que la del resto de tripulantes que vimos en el 'paddock' de SailGP lo decía todo. No poder brindar una alegría a la 'Marea Roja' que ha llenado los dos días las gradas montadas en la Marina es lo que peor llevan porque en realidad, siguen segundos en el Rolex SailGP Championship. "Y aumentamos nuestra ventaja con el cuarto (el Artemis sueco)", señaló Florian Trittel, el otro líder del equipo español, tratando de ver el vaso medio lleno aunque le costaba. "Después de lo bien que lo hicieron ayer se merecían más", añadía su mujer, que le esperaba para darle un abrazo y quien mejor sabe los sacrificios que implica el deporte de élite y lo que ha costado que 'Los Gallos' se instalasen en el olimpo de SailGP y hoy tuteen a una flota en la que hay leyendas de la vela como Peter Burling o Tom Slingsby, Con apenas 6 nudos de viento (11 km/h), la jornada tuvo que retrasarse casi 25 minutos y se recortó el recorrido. Las tripulaciones eran de cuatro en vez de seis, lo que implica mayor desgaste. Y En el caso de España la formaban Diego Botín, Florian Trittel, Joel Rodríguez y Nicole van der Velden. No subió mucho más el viento cuando se dio la salida de la primera de las dos mangas previstas y España pagó muy cara una mala salida. Su intención era hacerlo con buena velocidad por la zona alta de la línea de salida, buscando algún hueco para cruzar, pero los otros cinco barcos que formaban parte del Grupo B (Estados Unidos, Dinamarca, Francia, Canadá y Alemania) les cerraron y se quedaron los últimos. Cuando no hay viento, pagas aún más caro estar en esa posición porque te llega el 'viento sucio' de los otros barcos. Tocaba remontar y España ha demostrado que es capaz en muchas otras ocasiones, pero este domingo no se dieron las condiciones. Estados Unidos salió lanzado y puso un mundo de por medio con el resto de la flota. 'Los Gallos' y Francia no alzaban el vuelo y se quedaron rezagados. En la última ceñida, el equipo que lidera Botín tampoco tomó una buena decisión. "Hemos hecho una apuesta fuerte porque sabíamos que teníamos que pasar a un barco para quedar justo detrás de Dinamarca. Hemos intentado foilear pero no era lo acertado porque faltaba un poquito de viento y con los barcos que se nos han cruzado delante nos han dado un poco de desvente", explicó Botín. "Sabíamos que había posibilidades de que sólo hubiese una regata. Después de aplazarse la primera y con el tiempo que tenemos para las teles, ya veíamos que iba a ser complicado meter cinco (dos del Grupo A y dos del B más la final) en tan poco tiempo", explicó Nicole van der Velden, estratega del equipo español. "Salimos con la mentalidad de tener que darlo todo. En este caso nos habría gustado tener una más", añadió. El monólogo de Estados Unidos acabó con España sin puntuar y Dinamarca cuarta, lo que le dio dos puntos que le valían entrar para entrar en la final junto al equipo de Taylor Canfield. Del grupo A se clasificaron Italia como primera de grupo y Australia, segunda. En la final se impuso Estados Unidos. Aunque España ha acabado quinta en Valencia y ha roto su racha de podios esta temporada -llevaba siete en siete Grandes Premios en los que ha navegado porque se perdió dos por problemas técnicos- mantiene su segunda plaza de cara a la Gran Final de Abu Dabi (28-29 de noviembre), en la que competirán los tres mejores. Australia mantiene el liderato (85 puntos), seguida de 'Los Gallos' (68) y Estados Unidos (56). Y sólo quedan tres Grandes Premios. "Nos quedamos con una sensación un poco agridulce, después de tener un buen día ayer y estar en una buena posición. Pero seguimos ahí en la pelea por esa gran final de Abu Dabi", dijo. En Valencia, donde SailGP se ha estrenado este año y las colas para entrar en la Marina eran enormes a dos horas de comenzar el Gran Premio de España, se ha cumplido la maldición del equipo anfitrión. En las seis temporadas de SailGP, sólo Australia ha conseguido ganar los eventos en su casa (2019, 2022 y 2024). El próximo Gran Premio, el undécimo de la temporada, será en Ginebra (Suiza) los días 19 y 20 de septiembre. 'Los Gallos', que ganaron la temporada de 2024, quieren coser la segunda Copa en su camiseta, igual que las estrellas en el fútbol.

articles.title: Stoke attack 'now carries real threat'
articles.summary: BBC Radio Stoke commentator Mark Elliott reflects on Stoke City's 4-0 win at home to Charlton in the Championship.
articles.body:
First halves can't really go much better than Stoke's against Charlton.

Justin Devenny looked a proper player on debut, scored twice and provided a key pass for another goal, and George Hirst, the club's new first-choice number nine got off the mark too.

Ethan Galbraith has channelled his inner Paul Scholes during the early weeks of his Stoke career and got his third of the season, having never scored more than six in a campaign previously.

Galbraith looks like he could get double figures in goals this term, as does Devenny.

And Hirst did that in a very good Ipswich side last season, so a team that's been short on goals for a long time now looks like it carries a real threat.

That's despite losing more than 20 goals and assists from last season in the form of Sorba Thomas on deadline day.

If anything, the change to a back three brought about in part by his departure looks like it could symbolise the start of a new era.

The work done in the transfer window and the change in system has freshened things up and a 4-0 win has created belief in those changes on the terraces.

On paper at least, they face some more favourable fixtures over the next few weeks than those they had at the start of the season, so the Potters will have the chance to turn a great week into some real momentum.
authors: Mark Elliott - BBC Radio Stoke commentator

articles.title: Surprising win shapes Big 12 power rankings after Week 1
articles.summary: The top six teams in the Big 12 did as expected this week, but there was shuffling elsewhere as two teams turned in miserable performances.
articles.body:
It was the first full slate of games for Big 12 schools. Some of the contenders looked every bit the part, while others weren't exactly overwhelming.

Texas Tech and BYU, the teams that battled in the conference title game in 2025, registered convincing wins, while Houston, which came in nationally ranked, was less impressive in its win.

The biggest surprise was Oklahoma State, which lost to local rival Tulsa for a second straight year. While it wasn't a huge surprise last year, the Cowboys were thought to have been much improved with a new coach, one of the top quarterback additions from the transfer portal, and a roster full of newcomers.

Here are the Big 12 power rankings following Week 1. There wasn't much change up top, but the bottom half features some shuffling.

Will Hammond looked sharp, throwing for 298 yards and a touchdown in his return from last year's season-ending knee injury as the defending Big 12 champions looked the part. Texas Tech totaled 471 yards and limited the Wildcats to 194.

The Cougars led 56-0 in the third before giving up a lone touchdown. BYU has not lost to an opponent outside the FBS since 1960. BYU forced four turnovers, three before halftime, and held Utah Tech to only 52 yards in the first half and 184 for the game.

Connor Weigman threw for 305 yards, with Amare Thomas managing eight catches for 133 yards in a game that was closer than most expected. The nationally ranked Cougars were only up on the Beavers (2-10 last season) by a touchdown well into the fourth quarter.

The game was not expected to be close, and it wasn't. The Utes stormed to a 45-7 lead and never looked back. It marked the first win in the Morgan Scalley era. Utah racked up 633 yards of total offense and gave up just 255. It was a good start, but tougher challenges lie ahead.

Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita went 22-for-29 for 262 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats' season-opening win. The Arizona defense limited the visitors to 193 yards, 200 through the air. So yes, the Lumberjacks were a minus-7 on the ground.

Arizona State football kicks off 2026 season vs. Morgan State

Cutter Boley registered the best debut of any Sun Devil quarterback in school history by throwing for 387 yards and six touchdowns, despite coming out of the game five minutes into the third quarter. The ASU defense gave up just 188 yards, despite playing much of the second half with backups.

The Wildcats were a convincing winner in the debut of new coach Collin Klein, a former player at the school. Quarterback Avery Johnson went 15-for-21 for 199 yards and three touchdowns in his 27th career start at the school. Rodney Fields rushed for 101 yards.

Next up: vs. Washington State on Sept. 12.

Jacksonville State transfer Cam Cook rushed for 142 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries to propel the Mountaineers to a season-opening win. West Virginia broke in 88 new players. The win came despite West Virginia totaling fewer yards and first downs than the visitor.

It took a quarter for the Jayhawks to get rolling. They led 6-0 after the first quarter, but scored 24 in the second and were never threatened. Quarterback Isaiah Marshall went 14-for-19 for 246 yards and two touchdowns, while Nik McMillan had six catches for 130 yards.

Quarterback Julian Lewis was having a poor game until engineering a drive with 1:40 left that resulted in the game-winning points. The Colorado defense tried to give the game right back, but Georgia Tech missed a 45-yard field goal on the last play that would have won it.

The Bearcats only racked up 277 total yards, and 209 of that was on the ground. Nothing fancy, but the Bearcats got the job done in the first game of the post-Brendan Sorsby era. Six players factored into that rushing total, led by Hi'Bran Payne with 71 yards on 11 carries.

Next up : vs. Western Carolina on Sept. 12.

The Knights totaled 560 yards, 300 of that on the ground, in steamrolling the Wildcats. Ten ball carriers factored into that total, led by Duke Watson with 110 yards. UCF lost the shoutout on the last play of the game.

New quarterback Jaylen Rayner ran for two touchdowns and threw for two more as the Cyclones chalked up a win in the first game under new coach Jimmy Rogers, who was hired in December after veteran Matt Campbell bolted for Penn State. It has been a complete roster overhaul for Rogers, who has 81 newcomers.

The Cowboys parted ways with longtime coach Mike Gundy, got a highly coveted quarterback out of the portal in Drew Mestemaker, and the new coach brought a lot of his former players with him, only to lose to Tulsa, a two-touchdown underdog. Not a good start for the Eric Morris regime.

Was idle, but lost to North Carolina 15-10 on Aug. 29 in the opener

It's been a forgettable start to the season for the Horned Frogs on and off the field. Harvard transfer Jaden Craig had a tough debut at quarterback, going 20-for-32 for 175 yards. The offense totaled just 281 yards, 142 of that on 25 rushing attempts by Jeremy Payne.

Next up: vs. Grambling State on Sept. 12.

The Bears marched 70 yards in 14 plays and got within a point on a 5-yard scoring pass from D.J. Lagway to Gavin Freeman with nine seconds left. Coach Dave Aranda opted to go for the win rather than the tie, and the two-point conversion failed, leaving the Bears one point short. Freeman had 12 catches for 154 yards.

Next up : vs. Prairie View A&M on Sept. 12.

articles.title: MUST WATCH: Ainsley Maitland-Niles' sensational upper-90 Everton equalizer defies Manchester United
articles.summary: "Everyone wants to start off like that and thankfully I did," Maitland-Niles said after his stoppage-time goal to earn Everton a point vs Manchester United.
articles.body:
What a way to introduce yourself to Everton, Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

The 29-year-old had just joined the Toffees this week and subbed into the game for the final throes as Everton looked for its second equalizer of Sunday's Week 3 match versus Manchester United.

He sure did that, lashing a Goal of the Season contender from outside the box in the sixth minute of stoppage time.

"It's amazing," Maitland-Niles said after the game. "Everyone wants to start off like that and thankfully I did. The ball fell for me at the edge of the box, I put my foot through it and saw it go top corner."

"Felt like a win. We dug deep and managed to get a point at the end. The crowd was robust and fougth with us til the end."

articles.title: Joliet Catholic’s Caleb Smith, who believes ‘iron sharpens irons,’ comes up with big turnovers as a sophomore
articles.summary: Sophomore defensive back Caleb Smith has found the transition to varsity football to be a bit smoother than he expected at Joliet Catholic. But then again, S...
articles.body:
Sophomore defensive back Caleb Smith has found the transition to varsity football to be a bit smoother than he expected at Joliet Catholic.

But then again, Smith has been preparing for this for a while. It goes back to two summers ago, before he entered eighth grade, when Smith played on a team that won a United Youth Football League national championship in Plant City, Florida.

That team featured a host of kids who are now freshmen and sophomores in high school, including Armani Ford , who is starting at quarterback for Plainfield South as a sophomore and has the Cougars off to a 3-0 start.

"Going to Florida and winning that national championship was so fun," Smith said. "There are like 10 players from that team, who all go to different high schools, who are already on varsity and performing well.

"My dad always says that iron sharpens iron. When you play with guys who have a lot of skills, that definitely gets you ready."

Smith has certainly been prepared to step in as a starter this fall. He's already shown a knack for being in the right place at the right time. In a 21-14 victory over Springfield Sacred Heart-Griffin in Week 2, he recovered a fumble and then came up with a late win-sealing interception.

He produced another fumble recovery along with a few big tackles Friday night as the Hilltoppers dropped a 27-0 decision to rival Providence in New Lenox.

"I expected to maybe have a tough time with it being my first year on varsity," Smith said. "Surprisingly enough, I've been holding my own pretty well. I've been opportunistic.

"It seems like it's really hard to play in front of a lot of people and be in the spotlight, but after that first snap, I was able to get in focus mode, tune out the crowd and everything and just play my game. It's not as hard as I thought it would be."

While Friday night's score looks ugly, the Celtics (3-0) scored a touchdown on the opening kickoff and another on a 96-yard interception return at the end of the first half.

Defensively, the Hilltoppers (1-2) allowed just two TDs and mostly contained a Providence offense that ran wild in the first two weeks.

"We had some mistakes that let them score on us a couple times, but I think we're holding our own," Smith said. "When we were down, we had leaders who kept us playing hard and kept our eyes focused on the goal."

Joliet Catholic coach Jake Jaworski has liked what he's seen so far from his defense. And Smith in particular.

"He is a bright spot," Jaworski said of Smith. "You talk about competing, that's a kid who comes out and competes right from the get-go. I love his attitude. I love his demeanor. I love his confidence. He's definitely a kid who's a stud."

Smith discovered his love for football as a young kid, but only after he found a dislike for some other sports.

"My dad put me in like 20 different sports to see what I'd like and what I'd be good at," Smith said. "At first, it was basketball and baseball. But I started to hate baseball because I couldn't hit the ball and I'd get mad, so then I tried football.

"He saw how good I was at that and here we are."

Here Smith is indeed, making an impact for Joliet Catholic as a sophomore. And starting to believe in his ability to compete with the older guys.

"These first few weeks, getting some turnovers and everything, it's helped my confidence go up really high, knowing that I know where to be at the right time," Smith said. "I'm getting used to varsity.

"I'm getting the feel of it to help me for junior year, senior year, possibly even college."

articles.title: Four things we learned as Man United forced to settle for a point against stubborn Everton
articles.summary: 1 Man United hit the road once more, this time heading across to Merseyside to take on Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.After bouncing back from a poor...
articles.body:
Man United hit the road once more, this time heading across to Merseyside to take on Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

After bouncing back from a poor league start with a 2-0 defeat at Hull City, the Red Devils arrived in Merseyside after a sparkling 5-2 win over Ipswich, hoping to keep the momentum rolling with another important win against the Toffees.

But that was not the case. Man United left Merseyside with only a point after Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko saw their goals cancelled out by strikes from Tyrique George and Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

There was plenty to take from this match. Here's what stood out:

The false nine continues to hold Man United back

The absence of a clear number nine once again held United back.

Sesko understandably has not started yet after returning from a season-ending injury and missing a proper pre-season.

Yet after two cameo appearances against Hull and Ipswich, plus regular training, the Slovenian striker looks ready. He should have started against Everton and he showed that scoring from the bench.

His presence up top would have unsettled the home defence and turned those pinpoint Rashford crosses into genuine chances rather than wasted balls.

Matheus Cunha, as brilliant as he is, still isn't sparking the attack the way he can. Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford both suffer without a focal point to occupy defenders and open space.

United can only become truly threatening when someone occupies that number-nine role, pins the back line and creates openings for the runners around him.

The left wing looks genuinely threatening

In recent weeks, the left side had been a clear concern, with Luke Shaw often singled out as a weak link.

Against Everton, however, he delivered a solid defensive display and looked dangerous whenever he pushed forward.

He and Rashford are forging a real partnership down that flank. Shaw's overlapping runs and their constant link-up in the final third repeatedly caused Everton problems.

Rashford himself was a constant menace. The United forward kept taking on his markers, driving past them and creating clear chances. He proved a nightmare for the Everton defence, and Carrick's decision to place real trust in him is already paying dividends.

Man United appear to have lost one of their biggest weapons from last season. Casemiro's goals from corners are sorely missed, yet no one has properly stepped up to replace that aerial threat.

The Red Devils must rediscover their set-piece potency. It was their secret weapon last term, and it can still prove decisive this season.

Lammens once again failed to keep a clean sheet. He now has just three cleansheets in 14 games, a disappointing return given the high-quality performances he produces week after week. If United are serious about challenging for glory, they simply must start keeping clean sheets more regularly.

Drawing with Everton leaves United in a tricky position. They must respond, and they must do so quickly.

Next up comes their first taste of the Champions League league phase as they host Azerbaijani side Sabah Baku.

Just three days later the Manchester derby looms large, with Manchester City heading to Old Trafford for a Premier League matchday-four showdown.

Only by securing wins in these fixtures can Michael Carrick begin to silence the growing doubts over whether he is the man to take United back to the top.

articles.title: F1 Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli takes sensational home win from 19th at Monza
articles.summary: Antonelli defeats George Russell after a breathless comeback race in Monza to win the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has taken a sensational home win at the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix, coming form 19th on the grid to defeat Mercedes team-mate George Russell .

In an action-packed display of battery-led yo-yo racing, Antonelli overcame a grid penalty and a mid-race pitstop to scythe through the field and defeat long-time leader Russell, with Max Verstappen defeating McLaren to the final podium spot.

The race started with a huge blow for the sold-out, tifosi-filled grandstands. As shock polesitter Pierre held firm against Russell, Lewis Hamilton attempted to pass team-mate Charles Leclerc down the inside of the tight Turn 1 chicane, with Leclerc pushing the Briton wide on exit, costing Hamilton six positions as he dropped to ninth.

The incident was noted by race control, but on the end of lap 2 Leclerc suffered a huge crash on the exit of the final Parabolica corner as he fended off McLaren's Oscar Piastri . Leclerc skated across the gravel and veered into the outside wall at high speed, escaping unhurt but bringing out the red flag for lengthy barrier repairs.

Russell had been able to pass Gasly on the front straight earlier on the lap, ensuring the Mercedes driver would take the restart from pole, while Verstappen and Franco Colapinto worked their way up to third and fourth at the expense of Piastri.

All drivers were afforded a free tyre change under the red flag, with Verstappen the only frontrunner to pick mediums instead of hards. Following an extra formation lap for Yuki Tsunoda being out of position, Russell defended the lead from Gasly, while Colapinto passed Verstappen in the second Alpine for third. But after Verstappen retaliated with a trademark move around the outside of the second chicane, Colapinto went off the track in the first Lesmo right-hander, dropping the Argentinian down to 16th.

Kimi Antonelli fought Mercedes team-mate George Russell for the win

In the melee behind the pair, Hamilton moved up to fourth at the expense of Piastri, who was battling team-mate Norris and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad . After a rocket start, Antonelli took advantage of that fight to motor to sixth with a double pass on Norris and Lindblad on the main straight.

On lap 7, Alpine's hopes of a shock win for Gasly dwindled further when he was passed for second by Verstappen. Three laps later, the Frenchman also lost third to Hamilton, and he was powerless to keep Piastri and Antonelli behind as the Alpine man dropped to sixth.

Clearing Gasly quickly was supposed to hand Russell a clear path to victory, but on an afternoon where slipstreaming was key, the Mercedes man was unable to break away from Verstappen and instead starting coming under pressure from the Dutchman, with the pair trading the lead two more times on lap 12 and 15.

But rather than Russell, Antonelli quickly emerged as the more likely of the two Mercedes drivers to take victory despite starting from 19th. As the last driver of a gaggle of three cars, some two seconds behind the leaders, Antonelli had already picked off Hamilton and Piastri in quick succession.

Russell's jousting with Verstappen allowed Antonelli to rapidly close in on the lead battle, snatching second away from the Red Bull man on lap 16. Antonelli only needed one attempt to pass Russell for the lead, claiming control on lap 18 at Turn 1.

The so-called yo-yo racing, with battery levels dictating straight-line speeds, continued at a breathless pace, with Russell twice retaking the lead on lap 22 and 23. Suggestions from the pit wall to halt the yo-yo racing and build a gap to Verstappen were met with a grumpy reply from the young Italian, but he did comply as he tucked in behind Russell and conserved his more brittle medium tyres.

Lance Stroll was the second Aston Martin to retire

The story of the race changed when Lance Stroll ground to a halt in his Aston Martin, with Antonelli and Verstappen using the virtual safety car to rid themselves of their medium tyres and switch to new rubber. The pair came out in sixth and seventh, just 15 seconds behind Russell, who was nursing his hard tyres to the end.

By lap 37 of 53, Antonelli had worked his way past Hamilton and then Piastri to second place, giving himself 16 laps to close the nine-second gap to his leading team-mate while Verstappen followed him through into third.

Antonelli was quick but not initially catching Russell fast enough to close the gap, as the Briton escaped for action for a suspected yellow flag infringement. But Russell's hard tyres started showing worsening signs of wear towards the end of the race, allowing Antonelli to close the gap by the end of lap 47.

The first clash followed at the start of lap 49, with Russell cutting Turn 2 as he desperately tried to keep Antonelli behind. But the Italian went off as well, drifting through the gravel trap on the outside, allowing Russell to retain the lead.

Not best pleased by the Turn 1 skirmish, Antonelli tried again on the following tour but opted for a more straight-forward pass between Lesmo 2 and the Variante Ascari.

The 19-year-old held onto his hard-fought lead until the finish, winning his Italian Grand Prix home race at the second time of asking. Russell was a defeated second, with Verstappen joining them on the podium.

Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris scrapped in the closing stages

Piastri and Norris brought home fourth and fifth for McLaren at the expense of Hamilton, who dropped back on worn medium tyres to finish sixth. From pole, Gasly eventually salvaged seventh at the finish ahead of Lindblad and Colapinto, with the second Racing Bulls car of Tsunoda claiming the final point in tenth on his second weekend as a replacement driver.

In breathtaking fashion, Antonelli is the first Italian winner of the Monza race in 60 years as he reinforces his championship lead by seven points, now heading Russell by 66 points into next weekend's Spanish Grand Prix on the newly-built Madring in Madrid.

articles.title: Wrexham begin Adran Premier defence with big win
articles.summary: Wrexham begin the defence of their Adran Premier title with a comfortable win over Aberystwyth Town at The Rock.
articles.body:
Wrexham began the defence of their Adran Premier title with a comfortable win over Aberystwyth Town at The Rock.

Jenny Sugarman's side dominated the first half and Aber keeper Megan Bowen made vital saves to deny Katie Barker and Ava Suckley.

Natasha Thomas' effort struck the post and Maria Francis-Jones fired over the crossbar before the deadlock was finally broken on 32 minutes.

Thomas headed beyond Bowen from a Francis-Jones cross to score her first league goal since joining from Ipswich Town during the summer.

The hosts extended their lead with two quick goals at the start of the second half.

Francis-Jones scored with a sublime strike from just inside the area before Suckley netted from close range two minutes later.

Aber's attacks were few and far between, with Amy Jenkins' speculative effort from distance, which keeper Lucy Farrell gathered, their best effort.

Wrexham completed the scoring with Katie Barker's looping header from Lili Jones' cross finding the net.

Barry Town United 1-4 Briton Ferry Llansawel

Briton Ferry Llansawel began their Adran Premier campaign with an impressive win away to Barry Town United.

Goals from Maia Owen, Jade Crofts and Megan Kearle gave Ferry a commanding 3-0 interval lead at Jenner Park.

A second strike from Crofts after the break sealed the victory before Amy Long pulled a goal back for Barry with a penalty.

Lexi Jones and Fiona Barry scored as The New Saints won 2-0 away at newly promoted Cardiff Met.

Barry provided the assist for Jones, who scored from six yards out with just over 20 minutes remaining at Cyncoed.

Barry then got herself on the scoresheet wth five minutes to go, finding the net from the edge of the area.

Cardiff Met have returned to the Adran Premier after a season's absence after securing promotion with victory in the play-off final against Connah's Quay Nomads.

articles.title: Clemson Continues to Fall
articles.summary: Clemson continues to fall as they suffer a crushing defeat to LSU 51-10 Saturday night. It was the outcome many expected, but it looked much worse than we co...
articles.body:
Clemson continues to fall as they suffer a crushing defeat to LSU 51-10 Saturday night. It was the outcome many expected , but it looked much worse than we could've imagined.

Dabo Swinney's team looked completely outmatched, especially in the trenches. This was the largest deficit the program has faced in Swinney's tenure. Lane Kiffin's team looked every bit as good as advertised, while the questions surrounding Swinney's future in Tigertown will be amplified. Swinney must find a way to get his team to respond the rest of the season following this ugly loss.

The most glaring issue for Clemson was the offensive line. The offensive front was dominated by the LSU defensive line. Whether it was a run or pass, the Bayou Bengals were in the backfield on every play.

Chad Morris was brought in first and foremost to get the run game established on offense. Morris' offense accumulated negative four rushing yards in the first half because they could not create any movement up front. By the end of the third quarter, Clemson had 0 rushing yards. LSU finished the game with 11 total tackles for loss.

The Bayou Tigers also got it done rushing the quarterback, racking up four sacks against the Palmetto Tigers' offense. This made Christopher Vizzina's first start on the road a nightmare. He finished the game completing just 10 of 16 passes for 83 yards and an interception. Swinney attempted to throw Tait Reynolds in the game to generate something on offense. However, the offensive line could not protect well enough for it to matter.

Reynolds' first game of his college career ended with him completing four of his six pass attempts for just 22 yards. If Morris and offensive line coach Matt Luke can't get this group corrected, it will be a long season for Clemson. Nothing good can come from this offense if the line continues to play as badly as it did to start the season.

Flipping sides, the defensive front for Clemson was just as disappointing. LSU rushed for over 200 yards before halftime, and finished the game with 309 yards total on the ground. Running back Dilin Jones could not be stopped as he rushed for 113 yards and two touchdowns on the night. This was a result of the Clemson defensive front being unable to get any penetration.

Quarterback Sam Leavitt did not have the best day passing, but made a huge impact in the ground game as well . Leavitt had 113 yards rushing and two touchdowns as well, tying him and Jones as the top rushers for the game. As much as Leavitt struggled in the first half passing the ball, the success of the run game eventually opened things up enough for Leavitt to get himself a touchdown pass before the night ended.

The Bayou Bengals totaled 644 yards of offense against Clemson. Much of that had to do with Tom Allen's defensive line not being able to stuff the run or get pressure on Leavitt without extra rushers. Somebody on the defensive front needs to step up if this unit wants to see any improvement.

This was the worst-case scenario for Swinney's team to start the season. To get blown out in a primetime game makes this feel like the true end of an era for the Clemson program. It is clear this team is not a playoff-caliber team, which was already a far stretch for this group coming into this game. In week one, it's hard to know if LSU is that good or things have gotten that bad for Swinney's team.

The good thing is that next week's competition is not as stiff. Also, the game is at home as Georgia Southern comes to town. This team has got to drastically improve and find their stride over the next seven days, though. It will all start with finding ways to improve along the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. If the Tigers want to find any success this season, the offensive and defensive lines need to be better.

articles.title: Kai Trump’s College Debut Proves She Has the Work Ethic
articles.summary: Kai Trump makes her collegiate debut for Miami this Sunday at the Golfweek Fall Challenge in South Carolina. She will play as an individual after recovering...
articles.body:
Kai Trump makes her collegiate debut for Miami this Sunday at the Golfweek Fall Challenge in South Carolina. She will play as an individual after recovering from wrist surgery. The 19-year-old freshman is ready to show her work ethic, not just her name. This move signals a serious intent to compete at the highest amateur level.

Many people see the last name and assume the path is easy. The facts show a different story. She underwent surgery earlier this year "to address injuries to the stabilizing tissues of my ECU tendon and damage to my triangular fibrocartilage complex" on her left wrist. That is not a minor tweak. It is a major procedure that requires months of rehab. She committed to Miami in August 2024 and joined the 2026 signing class. Now she steps onto the course at Caledonia Golf & Fish Club. The 54-hole event starts Sunday and ends Tuesday.

Per Golfweek, she was not in the lineup when the Hurricanes won their first team event at the Boilermaker Classic. She missed that chance to win with her team. Instead, she waits for this specific moment to shine on her own. Her teammate Carlee Rogers will also compete as an individual. Scarlett Schremmer took the individual title at the team event, showing the depth of the roster. Trump has to prove she belongs there. The pressure is real.

On Friday, she poured in four birdies at a recent event. On the par-3 12th hole, she executed a tight draw that came very close to an ace. That is not luck. That is skill. Her massive social media following has helped her establish a brand as a golf influencer. Multiple NIL partnerships and her own clothing line are among her business ventures. The money is there. The fame is there. Now she needs the game to match.

The field at the Golfweek Fall Challenge is strong. Campbell competes in the field and has secured seven wins at this event. Last year, Charlotte won the tournament. These are not practice rounds. These are competitive events against players who want the win just as bad. The Hurricanes wear the orange, green, and white. They won their first team event earlier this week.

Kai Trump needs to win her individual battles to help the team. She has the brand power, but the course does not care about that. The ball still has to find the fairway. The putts still have to drop. Her debut at the Golfweek Fall Challenge is the first real test of her post-surgery game. If she can handle the pressure of a 54-hole event against top college talent, she proves she is more than a headline. The work she put in to heal her wrist is the only thing that matters now.

articles.title: Red Sox Send Confident Payton Tolle Message Before Orioles Finale
articles.summary: The Red Sox delivered a confident Payton Tolle message before the rookie left-hander’s important start in Sunday’s series finale.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox have put themselves in position to finish a dominant weekend in Baltimore. Now they are handing the baseball to one of the most important pitchers in their postseason plans. Boston celebrated Payton Tolle's scheduled start against the Orioles with a simple message Sunday morning.

" Tolle Bump Day! " the Red Sox posted on X.

The enthusiastic announcement captured the anticipation surrounding Tolle's 24th start of the season. It also served as a reminder of how quickly the 23-year-old left-hander has become a major piece of Boston's rotation.

Tolle enters Sunday's series finale with an 8-6 record, a 3.23 ERA and 147 strikeouts over 131 2/3 innings. Opposing hitters have batted just .220 against him, and his average of 10.1 strikeouts per nine innings illustrates the swing-and-miss ability that makes him especially intriguing in October.

His assignment at Camden Yards comes with Boston looking to complete a four-game sweep. The Red Sox won Saturday's game 5-0 behind seven scoreless innings from Sonny Gray. That followed a 1-0 victory Friday, giving Boston consecutive shutouts and three straight wins to begin the series.

A strong performance from Tolle could extend Boston's pitching dominance while moving the Red Sox another step closer to securing a postseason berth.

Payton Tolle Can Strengthen His Postseason Case

Tolle is coming off a less convincing performance against the Seattle Mariners.

The left-hander allowed four earned runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings Monday. Boston eventually won 9-8 in 10 innings, but the start continued a stretch in which Tolle has occasionally struggled to finish an otherwise effective outing.

Sunday gives him an opportunity to respond against an Orioles lineup that has been held scoreless for 18 consecutive innings.

Baltimore will counter with Kyle Bradish, who enters with a 7-12 record and a 4.01 ERA. Bradish has not earned a victory since July 22 and allowed 12 runs over his final 15 innings entering Sunday.

The pitching matchup appears favorable for Boston, but Tolle's performance could carry significance beyond one afternoon.

The Red Sox have arranged their September rotation in a way that could position Gray and Tolle to start the first two games of a potential Wild Card Series. Nothing has been formally announced, but their recent scheduling creates a clear possibility.

Gray looked ready for that responsibility Saturday. Tolle now gets his chance to offer an answer. Boston selected Tolle with the 50th overall pick in the 2024 MLB Draft. He reached the majors barely a year later and has since developed into much more than a promising rookie.

His combination of size, velocity and strikeout production gives Boston a weapon capable of taking over a short postseason series. The remaining question is whether he can consistently deliver deep, efficient starts when the pressure rises. Closing a road sweep would be another meaningful step.

First pitch between Boston and Baltimore is scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. The game will air on NESN.

articles.title: Fox News calls on Donald Trump after controversial college football call
articles.summary: On Saturday evening, the college football world was stunned after a controversial replay review gave the Michigan Wolverines one more second on the clock, al...
articles.body:
On Saturday evening, the college football world was stunned after a controversial replay review gave the Michigan Wolverines one more second on the clock, allowing them to score a touchdown on a Hail Mary and stave off an upset bid from Western Michigan. The incident became such a talking point that Fox News even wants Donald Trump to weigh in.

During Sunday morning's edition of Fox & Friends, the show's weekend hosts implored Trump to give his thoughts on the controversial call that has everyone riled up.

After getting largely outplayed the entire game, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood had one last chance to win the game for Michigan with a Hail Mary as time expired. Unfortunately for Michigan, the pass fell incomplete, and it appeared that Michigan had lost the game by a final score of 12-7.

Immediately after the play, the stadium announcer said it was under review. And a few moments later, the head referee stepped to the middle of the field and said, "After review, there's one second remaining in the game. Third down."

The problem is, none of the replays shown to viewers indicated that there should have been a second remaining on the clock.

Even NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay was confused as to what the referees were seeing to add a second back onto the clock, but Michigan was given one more chance, and they made the most of it. Underwood threw up another Hail Mary, and this time it was caught by JJ Buchanan to give the Wolverines a 13-12 victory.

After the game, the Big Ten issued a statement on the controversial decision:

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out -of bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling. Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned. Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-a, 'A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out of bound or that is on or outside a boundary line.' and thus the clock is stopped."

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out -of bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling.

Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned.

Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-a, 'A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out of bound or that is on or outside a boundary line.' and thus the clock is stopped."

Obviously, that did little to slow the debate and conversation.

Very curious what President Trump thinks'

During Sunday morning's episode of Fox & Friends, weekend hosts Griff Jenkins, Rachel Campos-Duffy, and Charles Hurt implored Trump to weigh in on the controversial call.

"I'm very curious what President Trump thinks about this," said Griff Jenkins. "He weighs in on sports. He weighed in on the World Cup red card.

"You think he has an opinion about this? Donald Trump has an opinion about this?" asked Hurt.

"I would be willing to bet when he wakes up," Hurt added.

"All night long, we're all checking Truth Social. We're all trying to see, 'when is he going to weigh in?' Mr. President, if you have an opinion on this, you can call in right now to the show. We want to hear what's going on," Campos-Duffy said.

Campos-Duffy then urged Hurt to "check again" to see if the president has weighed in.

"President Trump very often has his finger on the pulse of what our country's talking about, even if it's not in the political lane. This incident is going to be talked about for years to come," Jenkins said.

Jenkins said that the "entire country" is talking about the play and is eagerly awaiting Trump to weigh in.

"It's not just me; it's the entire country weighing in on that. So it will be interesting to see what the president ultimately, perhaps, has to say," Jenkins said.

"We'll keep checking. We'll keep you posted. The second the president weighs in on this, which we're certain he will," Campos-Duffy said.

articles.title: Everton 2-2 Manchester United: Late screamers share the spoils on Merseyside
articles.summary: Manchester United fell short of securing all three points on Merseyside on Sunday. Everton pulled out two screamers in the final minutes to equalize twice ag...
articles.body:
Manchester United fell short of securing all three points on Merseyside on Sunday. Everton pulled out two screamers in the final minutes to equalize twice against Michael Carrick's Reds in what could easily have been a second straight win. Instead, it's a third match in a row conceding two goals and more to ponder going forward about the defensive approach.

The Reds looked the better side for much of the contest. A first half of positive wing play did not produce many chances despite the exciting options up front. The best looks at goal came on a try for the spectacular by Bruno Fernandes and a ball across the box by Marcus Rashford.

Matheus Cunha was the one who got on the end of the ball from Rashford, but he sent the chance well over the target with his shot form the edge of the box.

United got on the scoresheet right after the restart though. After emerging from the dressing room at 0-0, Bryan Mbeumo got an opportunity to cut inside and fire past Jordan Pickford in the 46th minute. It was a low effort that beat the England No. 1 to his right side.

It appeared that the goal could spark a second-half flurry, but Everton settled in and began a long push for an equalizer. Senne Lammens was called to action a handful of times without the Blues finding a clear look at goal, and United's only real threat to double the lead came from another bit of Rashford magic. He skipped through the defense and somehow maintained the balance and poise to heel the ball to Cunha centrally, but James Tarkowski got a foot through the Brazilian's legs to poke the ball away before he could fire.

Everton's control of possession began to pin United back going into the final ten minutes. A clear instance of studs into Bruno Fernandes' ankle (which ripped his sock open to leave a visible mark) left the Reds defending with 10-men for a couple of minutes as well. Eventually the breakthrough came on a thunderous shot from Tyrick George. It was an effort neither Luke Shaw or Lammens seemed to expect, and fair enough because the angle was quite difficult. It didn't matter though, the power, pace, and placement of the hit was enough to beat the Belgian keeper at the near post and draw Everton level.

Carrick made most of his changes then. Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu had replaced Cunha and Rashford, and he sent on Andrey Santos and Leny Yoro after the equalizer. The Slovenian forward became one of the main characters of the final minutes, in both good and bad ways.

Shaw made up for his leniency defending George with a strong supporting run as United resumed the attack. Bruno found him on the overlap and he put a cross up in the air, hanging over the center of the box for Sesko to pounce and open his account for the season. He scored the winner on the road at Everton last year, and appeared set to do so again until late into stoppage time.

Everton got another screamer of an equalizer from Ainsley Maitland-Niles in the final seconds. What started as a corner led to some desperation around the edge of the box, and the winger popped up with space to fire a laser into the postage stamp corner of the goal. Sesko was the one policing the space at the edge of the box and didn't react in time to close the space afforded to the Evertonian.

The two goals conceded were rockets, but both were preventable. Fair enough for the beautiful strikes by Everton but United will feel they should have all three points. They'll need to reset with the start of the UEFA Champions League group phase on Thursday at Old Trafford, and then it's Derby Day next Sunday.

articles.title: NSL Week 18 and 19: BMO field curse broken, De Filippo heroics and record-breaking attendances
articles.summary: What a two weeks of Canadian football this has been. The Northern Super League (NSL) playoff race has been turned on its head, with Weeks 18 and 19 deliverin...
articles.body:
What a two weeks of Canadian football this has been. The Northern Super League (NSL) playoff race has been turned on its head, with Weeks 18 and 19 delivering yet again.

Week 18 belonged to Vancouver. The Rise stunned league leaders Ottawa 5–1 in one of their most dominant performances of the season. A week later, they followed it up with a dramatic 2–2 draw against Calgary. Those results helped Vancouver climb into fourth and put the rest of the league on notice.

Week 19, however, brought its own twist.

Montréal took advantage of Halifax's slip to move into first place, beating the Tides 1–0 in front of a record-breaking 17,000 fans at Stade Saputo. Meanwhile, Vancouver once again showed their ability to fight until the final whistle, rescuing a point against Calgary through Jess De Filippo's 95th-minute header.

In Toronto, the Battle of Ontario lived up to its name. AFC Toronto edged Ottawa 2–1 after a late fightback from the Rapid threatened to spoil the hosts' afternoon.

Vancouver stole the headlines in Week 18 with a five-goal demolition of Ottawa.

The Rise arrived at TD Place with plenty to prove and produced a performance that was impossible to ignore. After a cagey and physical opening half, Alex Lamontagne broke the deadlock in stoppage time on her first-ever NSL start.

Then came the avalanche (get it? Lamontagne… avalanche… never mind).

Lamontagne doubled Vancouver's advantage less than 20 seconds into the second half to complete her brace. Then, Anna Bout, Camila Reyes and Maithé López added three more. Ottawa eventually pulled one back through Elise Bell, but Vancouver had already done the damage.

Elsewhere, AFC Toronto beat Halifax 2–0 at Wanderers Grounds. Nikayla Small opened the scoring before Kaylee Hunter converted from the penalty spot. Toronto's defence did well to hold firm and secure the clean sheet. Sabs D'Angelo didn't falter between the sticks and Toronto managed the game brilliantly. Halifax pushed for a way back, but ultimately could not catch up. The final whistle confirmed a 2-0 away win for a team Halifax is yet to beat.

The weekend's final match saw Montréal and Calgary draw 2–2 in another rain-soaked battle. Taegan Stewart put the Wild ahead from the spot before Mimi Alidou equalized. Elyse Bennett then gave Montréal the lead early in the second half, only for Jorian Baucom to fire Calgary level.

The result kept Calgary's unbeaten run alive but Vancouver's rise was the biggest talking point.

If Week 18 was about Vancouver's surge, Week 19 was about the teams around them refusing to give up ground.

Montréal took a huge step to the top with a 1–0 victory over Halifax at Stade Saputo.

In front of more than 17,000 fans, the two sides battled. After a scoreless first half, the match eventually shifted in the 67th minute. Halifax's Sheyenne Allen was shown a second yellow card, leaving the Tides down to 10 players.

Mimi Alidou delivered a dangerous short corner and Anne-Valérie Seto rose to head the ball home in the 76th minute. Halifax pushed for an equalizer, but Montréal held on to claim the three points and now, the top spot.

Then came another Vancouver-Calgary thriller.

The Wild struck first through Serita Thurton, who was quick to react to a rebound. Shortly after, Vancouver's Quinn was brought down in the box. They equalized from the penalty spot with a powerful strike that almost seemed like it might go over.

Calgary restored its lead before halftime when Thurton's cross found Kahli Johnson, who headed home to make it 2–1.

Vancouver spent the second half chasing the game and eventually their persistence paid off when De Filippo was subbed on.

With 30 seconds left on the clock, it seemed like Calgary would be walking away with the win. Then, Reyes floated a ball in and Jess De Filippo rose to head it home in the 95th minute.

Another comeback. Another point. And another reminder that this Vancouver team will not go quietly.

AFC Toronto finally broke the BMO Field curse against Ottawa Rapid. They managed their first-ever win after their previous six matches there, including last year's championship final against the Rise.

After a goalless first half, Toronto finally broke through in the 71st minute. Kaylee Hunter curled a free-kick into the top corner. Hunter then helped create Toronto's second, setting up Sarah Stratigakis to make it 2–0 in the 85th minute.

Ottawa responded almost immediately through Florence Belzile, but Toronto held firm through the final minutes to secure three points.

The biggest takeaway from Weeks 18 and 19? There is no room for anyone to relax.

Vancouver's five-goal statement in Ottawa and last-gasp draw against Calgary have pushed the Rise firmly into the playoff conversation. Montréal's win over Halifax has reshaped the battle at the top, while Calgary's unbeaten run continues to make the Wild one of the league's toughest opponents.

AFC Toronto has also picked up crucial points, and Ottawa's position at the top is no longer as comfortable as it once looked.

With the table tightening and the regular season running down, the NSL has reached the point where one result can completely change the picture.

Two weeks ago, the standings looked one way. Now? It's all up for grabs.

articles.body:
Tennis fans cannot agree on one statistic after Coco Gauff's victory over Cristina Bucsa at the US Open.

Gauff defeated Bucsa in straight sets (6-3, 6-4) to reach the Round of 16, where she will face fellow American Iva Jovic.

It is the 19th time that Gauff has reached the last 16 of a Grand Slam in her professional tennis career.

Many would describe this as an outstanding achievement for a 22-year-old, but several critics have a different view.

Coco Gauff reaches another US Open Round of 16

Dozens of tennis fans commented on ESPN's social media post about Coco Gauff reaching the Round of 16 19 times.

One fan claimed that "she will save American tennis," and another suggested that she is a "potential GOAT."

"Coco is running a Hall of Fame career on a college schedule," said another, while a fourth wrote: "19 Round of 16s before turning 23 is insane consistency."

However, many others argued that the statistic highlights Gauff's consistent failures in the biggest matches.

The American is a two-time Grand Slam champion, but she has only reached three finals in four seasons as a top-ranked player.

"19 R16s is nothing special. Fans hyping basic stats like this make tennis so boring," commented an X user.

Two others posted that the Round of 16 "is starting to look more like a ceiling," and that "it just shows she folds early every slam."

While those comments were harsh, that comes with the territory of being a world-class athlete in the age of social media.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli charges through the field to win the Italian Grand Prix
articles.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli sliced through the field to win the Italian Grand Prix
articles.body:
There are days when you know you are witnessing something special.

That was Sunday at the Italian Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli, starting down in P19 Sunday at Monday due to a change in his power unit, rocketed his way through the field not just to take a podium finish, but to win outright and take a huge step forward towards winning his first Formula 1 Drivers' Championship.

His performance at Monza makes it seem like if he indeed wins a title this season, it will not be his last.

Antonelli carved his way through the field, working up to P12 for an early restart after a huge shunt from Charles Leclerc brought out a red flag on the third lap of the race. By Lap 9 Antonelli was up into sixth place.

By Lap 12 he was in a podium position, and he took the lead on Lap 18.

He would need to make another pit stop, as he started the race on a set of hard tires and made a switch to mediums during the red flag brought out by Leclerc's shunt. But when Lance Stroll came to a stop to bring out a Virtual Safety Car, Antonelli pitted for a fresh set of medium tires, coming back out in P6.

The stage was set for another charge to the front, and Antonelli quickly closed the gap to teammate George Russell at the front. The two battled for a few laps, with Antonelli finding the gravel at one point, but eventually he made his final overtake of the race.

Antonelli continued with the hammer down, recording the fastest lap of the race on the final lap of the race. With the victory, he became the first Italian driver to win the Italian Grand Prix in 60 years, as the last Italian Driver to win the Italian Grand Prix was Ludovico Scarfiotti, who won for Ferrari in 1966.

"I did not expect this," began Antonelli trackside after the race. "Unbelieveable. I'm so happy, I could have never imagined I'd be here today."

"After the second restart I was up there and I knew I had a shot for the win," continued Antonelli. "It was really difficult to break away, with the tow being so strong … nice to win."

The result felt like a death blow for Russell's championship chances. Starting in P2 and leading early, with championship rival Antonelli starting in P19, this was the kind of day Russell needed to maximize to increase his title hopes.

"Huge congrats to him. It was looking like a pretty strong race for us, but I was just struggling at the end on the tires," said Russell.

The result felt like something of a crowning achievement, as Antonelli not only maximized the result after starting at the back of the grid, but he actually extended his championship lead over Russell. Antonelli entered his home race enjoying a 59-point lead over Russell, but with the win he extended that lead to 66 points, with ten race weekends remaining.

Antonelli now has seven wins this season, and 11 podium results over 13 races.

articles.title: Antonelli claims epic win at Italian home GP after starting 19th
articles.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli had a sensational race as he charged from the back of the grid to claim an epic win at the Formula One Italian Grand Prix...
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli had a sensational race as he charged from the back of the grid to claim an epic win at the Formula One Italian Grand Prix on Sunday in front of his home crowd.

He's the first Italian to win at the Temple of Speed since 1966.

Antonelli started in 19th after he received a 30-place grid penalty due to a planned engine change. But following the restart after a long red flag period following a crash by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, the Italian was already sixth by lap seven.

His recovery culminated with a mid-race battle with team-mate George Russell. The two exchanged overtakes and Russell eventually came out on top.

The British driver got some breathing space after Antonelli pitted for new tyres on lap 29, while he stayed out after fitting a set of hard tyres during the red flag period.

In the closing stages of the race, Antonelli closed the gap and started his attack against Russell.

In a first attempt, he drifted onto the marbles at Turn 2 and then into the gravel. But with three laps remaining, he returned to the track, beat his team-mate and completed an epic win.

Russell had to settle for second, while Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third.

The race was interrupted for some 45 minutes after Leclerc of Ferrari crashed into the barriers at the end of lap two.

Leclerc started third with team-mate Lewis Hamilton in fourth as the Scuderia were bidding for a podium.

But they had a bad start as the two cars made contact once the lights went out and Hamilton was pushed off the track, dropping many places.

articles.title: Everton shrug off transfer window woes to hold Man Utd
articles.summary: Ainsley Maitland-Niles marked his Everton debut with a superb  strike with virtually the last kick of the game to snatch a 2-2 draw for the Toffees against M...
articles.body:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles marked his Everton debut with a superb strike with virtually the last kick of the game to snatch a 2-2 draw for the Toffees against Manchester United.

Maitland-Niles's arrival from Lyon on the final day of the transfer window was overshadowed by Everton's failure to reinforce their attack.

But the former Arsenal full-back lasered a long-range shot into the top corner in the 96th minute to punish a lacklustre United performance.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United in front inside the first minute of the second period.

But an Everton side short on attacking options rallied to level through Tyrique George.

Substitute Benjamin Sesko's header looked to have won United all three points.

But the decision not to reinforce Michael Carrick's defence will face more scrutiny as United have conceded twice in all of their opening three games of the Premier League season.

A draw maintains Everton's unbeaten start and keeps them one point ahead of United to calm the sense of unrest among the club's fans.

A miserable end to the window could still have ramifications for the teams performance over the rest of the season.

After letting Iliman Ndiaye depart in a £65 million ($88 million) move to Manchester City and Beto to leave for Fiorentina, the Toffees expected to strengthen their forward line with the signing of Monaco's Folarin Balogun.

An issue with the USA international's medical saw the clubs frantically renegotiate the structure of a £40 million deal but Balogun turned his back on the move.

David Moyes has been left with only one natural striker to pick from in Thierno Barry as a result and only 18 outfield players.

The return of Jack Grealish on loan for the season only slightly softened the blow as Moyes faces up to the realities of a possible relegation battle rather than a challenge for European football.

Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as United thrashed Ipswich 5-2 last weekend to get their season up and running after a dreadful 2-0 defeat at Hull.

The United captain came closest to breaking the deadlock in a first half otherwise devoid of quality when his volley came back off the crossbar.

A sleepy start to the second by Moyes's men proved costly as Mbeumo was allowed to bear down on goal on his favoured left foot and arrow a shot beyond Jordan Pickford.

United failed to build on their advantage.

The introduction of Grealish off the bench lifted the home crowd and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall twice failed to connect sweetly with clear sights of goal.

But the visitors' luck ran out seven minutes from time when Hayden Hackney fed George and the former Chelsea winger blasted into the top corner from a narrow angle.

Sesko's involvement has been limited at the start of the campaign due to an injury in pre-season, but the Slovenian looked sharp as he stooped to head in Luke Shaw's cross to restore United's lead.

The Red Devils never looked comfortable at the back but could not have foreseen the manner of the equaliser.

United looked to have cleared the danger with the five minutes of added time up, but the ball broke to Maitland-Niles who swept a curling shot into the top corner.

articles.title: Roma and Atalanta battle via statements on nasty D’Amico vs. Percassi row
articles.summary: Atalanta and Roma have released statements following the bitter argument between directors and former colleagues Luca Percassi and Tony D’Amico following the...
articles.body:
Atalanta and Roma have released statements following the bitter argument between directors and former colleagues Luca Percassi and Tony D'Amico following the dramatic Serie A match.

The Giallorossi scored twice in stoppages to overturn the Ederson strike, as Mario Hermoso and Matias Soulé secured a 2-1 victory at the Stadio Olimpico.

There was tension at the final whistle, including a red card for Dea midfielder Gianluca Gaetano, but it continued well after the match had concluded.

BERGAMO, ITALY – AUGUST 31: Luca Percassi, CEO of Atalanta BC looks on before the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Bologna FC at Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia on August 31, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

The tension was fuelled also by the fact that current Roma director of sport D'Amico had until a few weeks ago been working for the Bergamo side.

According to the Corriere dello Sport and Tuttomercatoweb , Percassi went towards D'Amico and began hurling insults, with the argument continuing all the way into the parking lot.

It was reported that D'Amico gave no response to the insults, and that security had to intervene to separate them.

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Mario Hermoso of Roma celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Atalanta BC at Stadio Olimpico on September 05, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

"AS Roma expresses its full support for Sporting Director Tony D'Amico in relation to the events that occurred following the match against Atalanta," read a statement.

"The Club considers the conduct of Atalanta CEO Luca Percassi towards one of its executives unacceptable and wishes to highlight the professionalism shown by D'Amico, who refrained from reacting in any way.

"AS Roma will refer the matter to the relevant sporting justice authorities for their appropriate consideration."

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of Roma, looks on before the Serie A match between AS Roma and Atalanta BC at Stadio Olimpico on September 05, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

Atalanta in turn released their own statement this afternoon , giving a very different version of events.

"Atalanta BC firmly reject the evaluation expressed by AS Roma towards CEO Luca Percassi. The Club, considering it opportune not to further fuel the matter via public comment, can declare itself entirely at the disposal of sporting justice investigations to verify the circumstances."

articles.title: Lane Kiffin on his haltfime wisecrack: "Everybody hates you. They can't hate you much more."
articles.summary: At halftime of Saturday night's 51-10 blowout win over Clemson, when LSU won 31-3, Tigers coach Lane Kiffin capped an on-field interview by saying, "Imagine...
articles.body:
At halftime of Saturday night's 51-10 blowout win over Clemson, when LSU won 31-3, Tigers coach Lane Kiffin capped an on-field interview by saying, " Imagine if we had pro players ."

After the game, Kiffin was asked about his halftime wisecrack.

"What's the difference?" Kiffin said. " Everybody hates you . They can't hate you that much more. So there you go. You got another line."

Kiffin took comfort in the fact that the NFL transfer storyline didn't loom over the outcome of the game.

"I'm just really glad they played the way they did, so that wouldn't have been the story," Kiffin said. "Because I get it . . . even if we won close and kind of ugly, the whole story would have been, 'Man, I screwed the team up by doing this.' And I said this morning, 'You can not agree with it. I've been criticized heavily for the last two weeks saying I did that.' . . . But my job is not to please you and worry about what you're going to write. My job is what I believe is right, and I believe we're fighting for what was right for those kids.

"I'm not going to get into all the reasons, but that's what I believe. And so many people don't like that, but they don't understand that."

Still, Kiffin knew or should have known that his effort to bring back players with NFL offseason and preseason experience would have sparked a backlash, especially at a time when the powers-that-be are looking for anything they can use to get Congress to clean up the mess that has flowed directly from the implosion of decades of antitrust violations.

They've been huffing and puffing about "pro players" returning to college football, while ignoring the fact that college football players have become pro players. They've been glossing over the fact that Nick Saban once brought an NFL free agent (Trent Richardson) back to campus to practice against college players. And they've been sinking their teeth into the disingenuous notion that the returning pro players will displace current players, ignoring the basic reality that current players get displaced all the time, by transfers and other incoming recruits.

Yes, he may be naturally inclined to wear a black hat. Or maybe he's just not afraid to do what's right for his team, even if the strategy plays directly into the hands of those who hope to parlay the current chaos into an antitrust exemption that allows player income to be restricted and player mobility to be limited.
