articles.title: Russell Explains the Fatal VSC Strategy Call That Stole His Victory: “Struggling on That One Hard Tyre”
articles.summary: For the vast majority of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix, George Russell appeared completely in control of his own destiny. After pulling off a sharp opening-lap...
articles.body:
For the vast majority of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix , George Russell appeared completely in control of his own destiny. After pulling off a sharp opening-lap move on pole-sitter Pierre Gasly and surviving the Lap 3 red flag triggered by Charles Leclerc's crash, the Mercedes driver looked poised to convert his front-row start into a commanding victory at the Temple of Speed.

Instead, a critical strategic gamble under a late Virtual Safety Car completely upended the race, leaving Russell defenseless on fading rubber while his teammate Andrea Kimi Antonelli charged from the back of the grid to snatch the win.

Mercedes opted for an extreme tire management strategy with Russell, keeping him out on a single set of hard compound tires following the early race stoppage. But when a late Virtual Safety Car period neutralized the field, the Silver Arrows pit wall was forced to make a high-stakes tactical call: preserve track position or pit for fresher, faster rubber.

While Russell remained out on track to protect the race lead, Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen both dove into the pits for fresh tires. The stark difference in grip proved decisive in the final laps, as Antonelli rapidly eliminated the gap and swept past Russell to claim an astonishing victory from 19th on the grid.

Speaking post-race, Russell admitted he never expected the team to bring Antonelli in.

"To be honest, I thought we were both going to stay out. I was surprised to see him pitting," Russell told the media. "I think in the end it was a roll of the dice both ways. You know, in the moment the team wouldn't have known which strategy was better. Made sense to split the cars, but in the end Kimi had great pace, and yeah, there we are."

The decision to stay out left Russell managing severe thermal degradation as the laps ticked down, leaving him a sitting duck on Monza's long straights.

"It was looking like a pretty strong race from us, and then I was just struggling with the tires towards the end," Russell explained to the media. "Obviously we did the whole race on that one hard tire, so yeah, I'll take it."

Despite the disappointment of missing out on top spot after leading so many laps, Russell was quick to praise Antonelli's historic drive from the rear of the field, noting that he spotted the Italian's rapid progress early on.

"Yeah, I mean huge congrats to Kimi, of course, incredible result from him," Russell said. "When I looked on the leaderboard at the beginning, I saw he was already in sort of P5, P4. I knew straight away he was going to be in the mix, so yeah, huge congrats to him."

While second place was a bitter pill to swallow given how close he came to standing on the top step of the podium, Russell emphasized that Mercedes' overall pace represents a significant step forward following the summer shutdown.

"It has been more positive than it was pre-summer break, and that's what I needed to try and achieve, but of course I would have loved to have been P1 today," Russell concluded.

articles.title: Which sub had biggest impact? Everton v Man Utd player ratings
articles.summary: How Everton and Manchester United's players rated at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
articles.body:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles crashed home a thunderous long-range shot as Everton scored in stoppage time to earn a 2-2 draw at home to Manchester United.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

Jordan Pickford: Not the busiest afternoon for the England keeper - might have done better for the goal. 6

Merlin Rohl (off 74, Hackney): Encouraged to get forward more by team-mates but seemed wary of leaving too much space behind him. Did provide the cross that Thierno Barry should have headed in. 6

James Tarkowski: Long ball straight to Senne Lammens in the second half drew groans from the crowd and a stream of invective from his manager. 6

Jarrad Branthwaite: Strong defensive performance, not afraid to get his body in the way of Man Utd shots and a brilliant tackle on Rashford. Found time to have a go at goal himself at the other end. 8

Vitalii Mykolenko: Found himself in space to create something inside the Man Utd box but failed to make the most of the opportunity. Got behind Bryan Mbeumo at the start of the second but again the outcome was poor. 6

Harrison Armstrong: Cautioned for needlessly dragging Bruno Fernandes round the neck, but a minor blot on an otherwise impressive performance. Easy to see why the Everton fans reacted so fiercely to the prospect of him being sold. 7

James Garner (off 76, Maitland-Niles): Decent effort against his old club. Worked tirelessly in defence and going forward. 7

Brennan Johnson (off 66, Grealish): Picked ahead of Jack Grealish but not the greatest game going forward. Blatant foul on Matheus Cunha earned a booking but probably worth it as it stopped the Brazilian racing into the box. 6

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: Industrious performance in the middle of the pitch went unrewarded in terms of result but would have been appreciated by boss David Moyes. 7

Tyrique George: Started well and lifted the ball over Mbeumo with superb skill. Drifted out of the game in the second half, until he beat Lammens. 6

Thierno Barry: Lucky not to be booked for a clear dive early on to try and win a penalty. Headed Everton's best first-half opportunity over from close range. Overhit a pass that could have sent Johnson through. 5

Jack Grealish (on 66): Ran at Diogo Dalot and drew a yellow card from the Man Utd man. Clearly determined to make an impact. His presence roused Everton's fans for a big finish. Tied Mbeumo in knots as he tried to set up an equaliser. 7

Hayden Hackney (on 75): Played the pass for the equaliser. 6

Ainsley Maitland-Niles (on 77): The decisive contribution. 8

Subs not used: Mark Travers, Michael Keane, Jake O'Brien, Tyler Dibling, Charly Alcaraz, Braiden Graham.

Senne Lammens: Made a mess of a routine ball into the box, although he had been impeded by Dewsbury-Hall. Aside from that, usual unflappable self. Saved the shots you would expect. 6

Diogo Dalot (off 84, Yoro): Another fortunate to escape an early yellow card for hauling back Tyrique George. Solid after that though and strong in the tackle. 6

Harry Maguire: Needed treatment for a bloody nose in the opening minutes but recovered and produced usual calm display. Partnership with Lisandro Martinez very effective. 6

Lisandro Martinez: Excellent effort from the Argentina defender. Positioning superb and didn't dive in for rash challenges. Got in the way of a Johnson shot as Everton pressed for an equaliser. 8

Luke Shaw (off 91, Mazraoui): Excellent effort and his fitness is so crucial now for Michael Carrick. Good block to stop an Armstrong effort and nipped in as Johnson was about to shoot. 8

Kobbie Mainoo (off 84, Santos): The usual smooth display, taking the ball and moving it on. Precise cross-field pass to Mbeumo led to the opener. 7

Youri Tielemans: Long-range effort didn't cause Pickford any problems. Went about his business quietly but still to see a stand-out performance. 6

Bryan Mbeumo: Quiet first half when a lot of his best work was in defence. Brilliant goal at the start of the second though. 8

Bruno Fernandes: Volleyed against the bar from a Mbuemo nod back, had another first-half effort deflected over and another blocked. 7

Marcus Rashford (off 70, Dorgu): Another eye-catching performance from the England man. Cunha wasted some of his excellent approach work. 8

Matheus Cunha (off 70, Sesko): Started in the number nine position and tried to exert influence but wasted an excellent chance midway through the first half. 6

Patrick Dorgu (on 70): Game went crazy after he came on. 6

Benjamin Sesko (on 70): Thought he had scored the winner here for the second season running. Needs to stay fit. 8

Subs not used: Karl Darlow, Mason Mount, Joshua Zirkzee, Ayden Heaven.

articles.title: Antonelli takes stunning Monza win from 19th on grid
articles.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli takes a breathtaking victory in an incident-packed Italian Grand Prix from 19th place on the grid.
articles.body:
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli took a breathtaking victory in an incident-packed Italian Grand Prix from 19th place on the grid.

The Italian caught and passed his team-mate George Russell, who started second, with three laps to go to extend his championship lead to 66 points.

Antonelli's performance is the second furthest back a driver has ever come from to win a grand prix after John Watson's victory from 22nd on the grid in the 1983 United States Grand Prix West.

It was a statement performance from Antonelli, who remarkably was on Russell's tail and challenging for victory within 16 laps of the start.

Antonelli looked capable of winning any which way, but decided to stop for fresh tyres under a virtual safety car mid-race and narrowed a 15-second gap to nothing before carving past Russell.

The Italian fans, who usually support Ferrari, rose to acclaim their new hero after a sensational drive as he crossed the line to take the chequered flag.

"I did not expect," Antonelli said. "Unbelievable. I am so happy, I could never imagine being here today."

Red Bull's Max Verstappen took the final podium place ahead of the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

The key stories of a gripping race at Monza were:

Antonelli's compelling and spectacular win, the best of a stand-out season from the Italian

A desperately disappointing day for Russell, who knew he needed to try to use this day to make up points on his team-mate

A disappointing home race for Ferrari, with Lewis Hamilton finishing sixth and Charles Leclerc crashing out early

Antonelli again comes out on top of Mercedes battle

The day started with Antonelli looking to limit the damage inflicted on his points lead by Russell as he started at the back of the grid because of a penalty for using more than his permitted number of engine parts.

An early stint of cautious, measured attacking lifted Antonelli up to 12th place on the third lap when Leclerc lost control at the Parabolica after getting slightly wide defending from Piastri, smashing deep into the barriers and bringing out the red flag.

Leclerc was unhurt and the race was stopped while the marshals rebuilt the barriers at the famous final corner.

By this time, Russell had taken the lead from shock pole winner Pierre Gasly's Alpine and looked in control of the race.

But the restart saw a compelling series of laps as the leading drivers ran nose to tail and Antonelli picked his way through the pack and into contention.

Four laps after the restart, Russell was leading a six-car train with Antonelli at the rear. Gasly started to drop back and the Italian moved past the Frenchman, Hamilton and finally Piastri before joining a three-car battle for the lead with Verstappen.

The Dutchman briefly took the lead from Russell on lap 11, before the Briton re-passed him three laps later, Antonelli overtaking the Red Bull into the second chicane.

From laps 17 to 24, the Mercedes battled hard, the two passing and re-passing each other as they played with the boost and overtaking modes in the new hybrid engines as Verstappen sat right behind them with the best seat in the house.

Antonelli was then told that Russell had been asked to push and build a gap to Verstappen, and the tension was betrayed in Antonelli's response, when he asked if they wanted him to sit back and not challenge.

Shortly afterwards, a virtual safety car was called when Lance Stroll's Aston Martin broke down at the first chicane and Antonelli's side of the garage decided to risk a stop for fresh tyres. Russell stayed out, needing to nurse his tyres to the end, and Verstappen followed Antonelli in.

Antonelli rejoined in sixth place and 15 seconds behind his team-mate, but he moved past Gasly, Norris, Hamilton and Piastri as he closed in on his team-mate.

Russell began to struggle with his tyres as Antonelli homed in and by lap 48, with five to go, the two were nose to tail.

An initial attempt into the first chicane on lap 50 came to grief when Antonelli got on to the rubber debris off line turning into the second part of the first chicane and slid into the gravel.

But such was his pace advantage that he soon closed the 1.7-second gap that had opened up and easily breezed past Russell on the run between the Lesmo corners and Ascari.

A resigned Russell said: "When I looked at the leaderboard a few laps after the restart and saw he was already in P5/6 I knew he would be in the mix. I was just struggling with the tyres at the end.

"I will take it. It has been more positive than before summer break but of course I would have loved to be P1 today."

Leclerc shattered by error as crash follows Hamilton contact

Ferrari's day to forget started when Leclerc barged Hamilton on to the grass exiting the first chicane on the opening lap, the seven-time champion dropping to 10th.

Leclerc then challenged Gasly for third on lap two before being passed by Verstappen into Ascari.

That slowed his exit, and left him vulnerable to Piastri, who attacked on the inside into Parabolica.

Leclerc was slightly wide on entry and through the apex, and that carried his left rear tyre wide onto the white line on the edge of the track, and partly over the artificial grass section before the gravel trap.

There, the car lost grip, and a high-speed tank-slapper spun Leclerc into the barrier at high-speed.

After climbing from the car, he sat down behind the barriers, his head bowed, shattered by his error.

Hamilton recovered well initially, with a strong restart moving him up to fourth within two laps.

But the Ferrari's lack of straight-line speed was ultimately costly and he slipped behind Antonelli and the McLarens as the race wore on.

Verstappen impressive as Norris gets Piastri at end

Everyone was put in the shade by Antonelli's superlative drive, but Verstappen was impressive in moving up from sixth on the grid to third in the Red Bull and fighting for so long with the Mercedes.

In the end, he could not hold on to the silver cars and his stop drop him behind Piastri, Hamilton and Norris.

His fresher tyres helped him move back into third place but he could go no further.

Behind him, Norris began to move up as the race went on, and he passed Hamilton before moving on to the back of a three-car train behind Verstappen and Piastri.

Norris looked to make a move on Piastri in the closing laps but the Australian eased him over to the grass on the outside of the exit of Curve Grande as Norris went for the inside approaching the second chicane.

Norris complained he had been pushed off, and the team warned Piastri to race clean, but Norris finally did make it past on the final lap.

Gasly was never going to hold on to the lead, and the Alpine's lack of pace after his stunning qualifying performance, aided by compromises elsewhere, soon began to tell.

But seventh is a good result as Alpine went into the race aiming mainly to ensure they finished ahead of the Racing Bulls, their rivals for fifth in the constructurs' championship.

Gasly succeeded, but Arvid Lindblad beat the second Alpine of Franco Colapinto to eighth place as the second Racing Bulls driver Yuki Tsunoda completed the top 10.

articles.title: Maitland-Niles stuns Manchester United as Everton claim last-ditch point
articles.summary: Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko goals cancelled out as Everton come from behind to win point in 2-2 draw with United.
articles.body:
Ainsley Maitland-Niles ‌scored a brilliant equaliser on his debut with virtually the last kick ⁠of the game as ⁠Everton rescued a point in a 2-2 Premier League draw with Manchester United at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, England.

Benjamin Sesko looked to have won ⁠the football game for the visitors with an 87th-minute header in Sunday’s game, but substitute Maitland-Niles hit a first-time shot from 30 yards to preserve his side’s unbeaten start to the season.

United have ⁠four points from their opening three games of the campaign and lie in 11th place in the Premier League standings, while Everton are in eighth with five points from the same number of matches.

Bryan Mbeumo’s superb solo effort had put the visitors in front early in the second half, ‌but Everton grew steadily into the game and Tyrique George equalised with a ferocious shot, before the late goals from Sesko and Maitland-Niles.

United will be disappointed not to have taken the three points in a game in which they led twice and struck the bar in the first half through Bruno Fernandes.

But Everton had the better of the attacking chances, with more shots on target. They kept plugging away, showing the ⁠kind of fighting spirit they will need this season with ⁠their wafer-thin squad following a much-criticised transfer window.

Matheus Cunha blazed over from a good position, while the best chance of the first half fell to Everton striker Thierno Barry from Merlin Rohl’s superb cross from the right, ⁠though he put his free header over the bar.

It took United a minute to score in the second period when Mbeumo ⁠was able to cut inside from the right and place ⁠his left-footed shot from the edge of the box into the far corner.

James Tarkowski’s excellent last-ditch tackle on Cunha denied the Brazilian a goal, before Everton introduced Jack Grealish in the 66th minute as he began a ‌second loan spell on Merseyside and made a difference to their attacking cohesion.

George thundered the ball past United goalkeeper Senne Lammens at the near post to equalise in the 82nd ‌minute, ‌before Sesko looked to have won the game when he headed in Luke Shaw’s cross, until Maitland-Niles came up with his moment of magic at the death.

articles.title: No. 16 Michigan escapes an ‘epic loss’ thanks to a disputed replay and a second-chance Hail Mary
articles.summary: Bryce Underwood watched his pass sail out of bounds, and he thought he knew what that meant for No. 16 Michigan.
articles.body: ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Bryce Underwood watched his pass sail out of bounds, and he thought he knew what that meant for No. 16 Michigan. “I definitely thought the game was over because there were zeroes on the clock,” he said. So did Western Michigan. So did a lot of people watching. Given a second chance by a disputed replay decision, Underwood and the Wolverines took advantage. JJ Buchanan pulled in Underwood’s 47-yard, second-chance miracle heave for a game-ending, game-winning touchdown, and Michigan escaped with a 13-12 win over the Broncos on Saturday night in coach Kyle Whittingham’s debut. On what seemed to be the final play of the game, Underwood chucked a Hail Mary pass that sailed beyond the end zone and into the arms of a Broncos defender. TV replays appeared to show the clock hitting zero with the ball still in the air, but officials ruled there was a second still to play. The Big Ten stood by the review in a statement released two hours after the game, when it also published a recording of the replay as it was reviewed by the officials that showed the game clock at 1 second when the ball was touched by WMU’s Micah Davis. “It was determined Western Michigan No. 18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock,” the conference said, citing rule that stops the clock on such contact. Mid-American Conference Commissioner Jon Steinbrecher said the conference and school contacted the Big Ten office, seeking clarification on the review and was provided with an explanation along with video and audio that confirmed it. Steinbrecher thanked the Big Ten for its prompt response. The call gave Michigan new life. “We were flirting with disaster, and that would’ve been an epic loss,” Whittingham said. Indeed, Michigan fans were already having flashbacks to a season-opening loss to Appalachian State in 2007, when the Wolverines faltered as 33-point favorites. They were projected to win by 27 1/2 points over the Broncos but had to experience momentarily watching WMU celebrate the victory at Michigan Stadium before the replay decision made the winning score possible. Michigan fans stormed the field after the win, but the team was hardly in the mood for a party. “Sick to my stomach is the way I explain my feelings about that game,” defensive end Dom Nichols said. Whittingham said he thought there was a second left on the clock, while Broncos coach Lance Taylor said he hadn’t seen a replay before speaking to reporters. Underwood took advantage of another chance to win the game, and redeem himself from a poor performance, with Buchanan leaping to snag the football and coming down with it in the end zone. “We practiced it three or four times over the last month,” said Underwood, who added it was “a blessing” to have another second put back on the clock. Whittingham was hired to stabilize a program reeling after the firing and arrest of Sherrone Moore, who held the job for just two seasons following Jim Harbaugh’s tenure that included a 2023 national title along with a spying scandal and NCAA sanctions for recruiting violations. There hasn’t been much drama off the field, but this was hardly an encouraging start on it. “That was a moment we don’t really want to be living,” Nichols said. Michigan will have to improve quickly to compete next week with No. 10 Oklahoma at home. “If we don’t play a lot better, it’s not going to be pretty,” Whittingham said.

articles.title: Cardinals, Rockies players tilt caps a day after umpire’s comments to St. Louis rookie
articles.summary: St. Louis and Colorado players tilted their caps Saturday in apparent protest of umpire Doug Eddings one day after he told Cardinals rookie Hancel Rincon to straighten his hat.
articles.body: Players from St. Louis and Colorado tilted their caps Saturday night in apparent protest of umpire Doug Eddings one day after he instructed Cardinals rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to straighten his hat. Eddings’ comments prompted an argument with St. Louis manager Oliver Marmol that led to Marmol’s ejection. Most of the Cardinals’ players had their hats tilted during pregame warmups, and many continued to tilt them in the dugout during the game. Some even tilted their batting helmets to celebrate reaching base. At least some Colorado players also wore their caps to the side. Rincon said Eddings apologized to him when they spoke briefly on the field Saturday. Rincon said through an interpreter that he accepted that apology. Eddings also spoke to Marmol before the game, but the manager said there was “nothing of meaning” out of their brief conversation. “We’ve had a few rough stretches here, but the one superpower that we’ve had through this whole season is our ability to unify and really stand up for all the guys we have in the clubhouse and have each other’s backs,” Matthew Liberatore, St. Louis’ starter Saturday night, said after the Rockies’ 10-5 win. “It’s a really tight-knit group. I love the fact that regardless of what’s going on, they always have each other’s backs,” Marmol said. Rincon, a 24-year-old from the Dominican Republic, made his major league debut in relief in the sixth inning Friday night and wore his cap with the brim pointing to the left. He straightened it at Eddings’ urging, then got Hunter Goodman to fly out before TJ Rumfield tripled and scored on a wild pitch and Cole Carrigg hit an inside-the-park home run. Rincon allowed another single before being replaced by Justin Bruihl. Marmol then came out of the dugout to confront Eddings and was ejected during Colorado’s five-run inning. “I had an issue with Doug,” Marmol told reporters after the game. “Just Doug. He took it upon himself to tell our rookie pitcher the kid’s ‘not going to wear his hat on my field that way.’ You got Dontrelle Willis, CC Sabathia, Pedro Strop – plenty of guys that have worn it way more tilted. I have an issue with that. That’s just a power-hungry move, in my opinion.” Eddings told reporters postgame that he confronted Rincon after a Colorado hitter complained. Goodman was the only hitter to face Rincon at the time of the warning, and the catcher told MLB.com on Saturday that he did not complain to Eddings. St. Louis rallied to win 7-6 on Friday after Ivan Herrera’s three-run homer in the ninth inning.

articles.title: El sorpresivo exjugador que Alberto Gamero quiere como su asistente en Millonarios
articles.standfirst: Faryd Mondragón suena con fuerza como asistente de Alberto Gamero en Millonarios
articles.summary: Faryd Mondragón suena con fuerza como asistente de Alberto Gamero en Millonarios
articles.body: El regreso de Alberto Gamero a la dirección técnica de Millonarios no solo ha significado ilusión y expectativa entre la hinchada albiazul, sino que también ha empezado a mover las fichas y sacudir el entorno del cuerpo técnico. En medio de los cambios y ajustes para enderezar el camino del equipo en la Liga BetPlay, un nombre inesperado y de mucho peso comenzó a sonar con fuerza en las últimas horas: Faryd Mondragón. Según revelaron diversos sectores periodísticos deportivos, el histórico exarquero de la Selección Colombia y actual comentarista de televisión es el principal candidato que tiene en mente el entrenador samario para sumarse como uno de sus nuevos asistentes técnicos. La noticia ha tomado por sorpresa a propios y extraños. Desde su retiro como profesional en 2014 —tras disputar la Copa del Mundo en Brasil y convertirse en su momento en el jugador más longevo en pisar una cancha mundialista—, Mondragón se ha mantenido ligado al balompié principalmente desde los medios de comunicación, destacándose como analista y panelista en espacios televisivos. Sin embargo, la posibilidad de dar el salto al banquillo como parte del staff técnico de un grande del país ha puesto al exguardameta en el centro de la conversación nacional. De concretarse su llegada, Faryd se integraría al grupo de trabajo junto a Jorge Castro (quien también hace parte del equipo de asistentes de Gamero) y el preparador físico Julio Charales, en una estructura que prescindiría de otros nombres que se habían barajado inicialmente como Orlando Rojas o Felipe Palmezano. La información generó rápidamente debate entre los seguidores del conjunto bogotano. Por un lado, se destaca la jerarquía, la vasta experiencia internacional y el liderazgo que un exmundialista de la talla de Mondragón podría inyectarle al camerino y al proceso formativo de los arqueros y jugadores jóvenes. Por otro lado, al tratarse de lo que sería su primera gran experiencia directa en la dirección técnica de campo, un sector de la hinchada mantiene reservas sobre cómo se acoplará a la exigencia del día a día en una institución con la presión y la historia de Millonarios. Mientras los rumores sobre la conformación definitiva del cuerpo técnico siguen tomando fuerza y se espera una confirmación oficial por parte de la directiva del club, Alberto Gamero ya se encuentra enfocado en el terreno de juego. El estratega samario asumió nuevamente las riendas del equipo con la firme misión de recuperar la regularidad, imprimirle su sello futbolístico al plantel y volver a posicionar al cuadro embajador en la pelea por los títulos del fútbol colombiano. El tiempo dirá si la experiencia de Faryd Mondragón se suma finalmente desde la raya para aportar su granito de arena en este nuevo ciclo albiazul.

articles.title: Preocupación por 'Cochise' Rodríguez: internan de urgencia a la leyenda del ciclismo
articles.standfirst: Martín "Cochise" Rodríguez, hospitalizado en Medellín: cuál es el estado de salud del exciclista
articles.summary: Martín "Cochise" Rodríguez, hospitalizado en Medellín: cuál es el estado de salud del exciclista
articles.body: El deporte nacional se mantiene atento a la evolución médica de Martín Emilio ‘Cochise’ Rodríguez, uno de los máximos íconos e históricos del ciclismo en Colombia, quien debió ser internado en un centro médico de la ciudad de Medellín tras presentar problemas de salud. De acuerdo con la información entregada por sus familiares, el excampeón mundial ingresó al centro asistencial luego de manifestar mareos e insuficiencia cardíaca. Jesús Piedrahíta, directivo del equipo Orgullo Paisa, señaló a medios locales que el exdeportista se encuentra bajo estrictos chequeos médicos según los reportes de su esposa. A pesar de la alerta inicial, el propio ‘Cochise’ llevó tranquilidad a sus seguidores a través de una conversación telefónica en la que confirmó que su estado actual es estable y que se encuentra enfocado en su recuperación. “Aquí recuperándome de un problemita en el mango (corazón), es algo muy leve y creo que no tendré que quedarme acá hospitalizado por mucho tiempo”, expresó el ex pedalista, mostrando el optimismo que siempre lo ha caracterizado. Martín Emilio ‘Cochise’ Rodríguez es considerado un verdadero pionero y pilar fundamental del ciclismo colombiano. Antes de labrar una carrera llena de glorias y abrirle las puertas a los ciclistas nacionales en Europa —llegando a competir en prestigiosos equipos como el Bianchi—, ‘Cochise’ se ganaba la vida trabajando como mensajero en bicicleta. Entre sus múltiples e inolvidables palmarés destacan: El entorno del deporte nacional y los aficionados esperan su pronta recuperación para que esta gran leyenda del ciclismo continúe recibiendo el cariño y homenaje de todo un país.

articles.title: El emotivo homenaje a Ale Salazar en Madrid: “He disfrutado como una niña”
articles.standfirst: El torneo reconoció a la madrileña, que esta semana jugó por última vez en casa. El momento de más emoción en su abrazo con Triay.
articles.summary: El torneo reconoció a la madrileña, que esta semana jugó por última vez en casa. El momento de más emoción en su abrazo con Triay.
articles.body: El torneo Comunidad de Madrid P1 rindió un sentido homenaje a Alejandra Salazar (Madrid, 40 años), quien esta semana jugó por última vez en su casa (junto a Aranza Osoro alcanzó los cuartos de final, donde cayeron ante Triay y Brea). "Pensar que hace 30 años, cuando era una niña, iba a entrenar y me preguntaban: '¿Te vas a jugar al tenis?'. Y yo les decía: 'No, al pádel'. Y me respondían: '¿Al pa qué?'. Y mira, hoy estamos aquí en Madrid siendo 15.000 personas, y la semana próxima estaremos en todos lados. Me llevo la tranquilidad de que he aportado mi granito de arena para que hoy estemos aquí y el pádel esté donde se merece", fueron las primeras palabras de Ale al tomar el micrófono. La ceremonia comenzó con Salazar transitando un pasillo formado por su familia, amigos y personalidades del pádel que han marcado su carrera: desde sus primeros entrenadores hasta su pupila Claudia Fernández; Carolina Navarro, la compañera con la que fue número uno por primera vez; y Gemma Triay, quien la ayudó a forjar su leyenda. Fue justamente ese momento, ese abrazo y ese primer plano, el de mayor emoción de la jornada. "He disfrutado este camino como una niña pequeña. Gracias al pádel por todo", sintetizó. Su retirada se hará efectiva a final de año, con la esperanza de clasificarse a las Finals de Barcelona (actualmente se encuentra entre las 16 mejores, pero su plaza dependerá de los resultados que obtenga en el cierre de la temporada). Además, está en juego su convocatoria con la selección española para el Mundial de Qatar, certamen que la consagra como la máxima ganadora de la historia con siete títulos.

articles.title: Shakira hace historia: "Dai Dai" supera los mil millones de reproducciones y rompe récords
articles.standfirst: "Más allá de mis sueños": Shakira celebra histórica cifra de reproducciones con 'Dai Dai'
articles.summary: "Más allá de mis sueños": Shakira celebra histórica cifra de reproducciones con 'Dai Dai'
articles.body: La superestrella colombiana Shakira ha vuelto a reescribir las páginas doradas de la historia de la música contemporánea. Su exitoso sencillo 'Dai Dai', interpretado en colaboración con el artista nigeriano Burna Boy y consolidado como el himno oficial del Mundial de Fútbol 2026, ha alcanzado la astronómica cifra de mil millones de reproducciones en las plataformas digitales. Este nuevo hito no solo ratifica el impacto ininterrumpido de la barranquillera en la industria global, sino que la posiciona nuevamente en la cima del pop mundial, evocando aquel histórico precedente que marcó en 2010 con el inolvidable Waka Waka. El camino hacia el billón de reproducciones de "Dai Dai" comenzó a labrarse el mismo día de su lanzamiento. Desde sus primeras 24 horas en el mercado, el sencillo rompió marcas al superar los 10 millones de visualizaciones en YouTube y escalar de manera meteórica hasta la posición número uno de las tendencias globales. La mezcla de ritmos urbanos, la frescura de la propuesta musical y la participación de Burna Boy conectaron de forma instantánea con audiencias de todos los continentes. La producción audiovisual, grabada íntegramente en Miami, destacó por un despliegue visual impresionante que incluyó canchas urbanas, estadios mundialistas y cameos estelares de leyendas y referentes del fútbol internacional como Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane, Vinícius Júnior y el colombiano Luis Díaz. Ante la abrumadora cifra alcanzada, la intérprete de éxitos mundiales no ocultó su emoción y agradecimiento hacia sus seguidores. A través de sus redes sociales, Shakira compartió un mensaje que resonó profundamente en su legión de fanáticos: “Mil millones de reproducciones están más allá de mis sueños. Gracias a mis increíbles fans por hacer todo posible. ¡Los amo!” Para la artista, este logro representa la culminación de un trabajo que buscó trascender el ámbito deportivo para convertirse en un mensaje universal de unión, alegría y superación personal, dedicado especialmente a inspirar a las nuevas generaciones. El impacto de "Dai Dai" trasciende los récords de reproducción y el éxito en listados como Spotify y YouTube. El fenómeno musical ha ido de la mano de iniciativas solidarias de gran envergadura. Sony Music y la propia Shakira anunciaron en su momento planes de apoyo benéfico, destinando fondos e igualando donaciones destinadas a causas como el Fondo de Educación de Global Citizen, vinculado también a las entradas de su gira mundial Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran Tour. Con este nuevo récord, Shakira reafirma su estatus de leyenda viva de la música latina, demostrando que su capacidad para reinventarse, conectar con públicos multiculturales y dominar los escenarios internacionales sigue más intacta y vigente que nunca. Mientras se prepara para una nueva e intensa etapa de conciertos en directo, "Dai Dai" ya queda grabado en la memoria colectiva como uno de los grandes hitos musicales de la década.

articles.title: F1 leader Kimi Antonelli wins Italian GP after epic charge from the back
articles.summary: Antonelli’s sensational race from 19th to the win at Monza makes him the first Italian to claim the title in 60 years.
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has delivered one of the most sensational triumphs in the long history of the Italian Grand Prix by becoming the first home winner in 60 years after starting from 19th on the grid.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver, from nearby Emilia-Romagna, claimed his seventh win of the season on Sunday to extend his lead in the drivers’ title race as he seeks to become Italy’s first world champion since Ferrari’s Alberto Ascari in 1953.

He is the first domestic winner of the Italian GP since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

In a thrilling, helter-skelter race of wild overtaking moves, Antonelli came home 3.857 seconds ahead of his teammate and title rival George Russell, who is now 66 points adrift in the championship, with four-time champion Max Verstappen third for Red Bull.

For the impassioned Italian crowd, his win was some consolation for their disappointment in seeing Ferrari endure a disappointing flop with Charles Leclerc crashing out on lap two, and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton finishing sixth behind the McLaren pair of world champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli had started at the back of the grid after taking penalties for power-unit changes, but showed searing pace throughout as he carved through the field – benefitting from an early red flag stoppage – before outracing Russell to win.

“Unbelievable!” said an emotional Antonelli.

“I’m so happy, I could never have imagined being here today, but we pulled it off.

“After the second restart, I knew I was up there and could have had a shot at the win.

“I believed in it, especially when I was behind George, but it was really difficult to break away with the tow being so strong.”

Alpine’s maiden pole-sitter Pierre Gasly finished seventh ahead of Racing Bulls’ rookie Arvid Lindblad, Franco Colapinto in the second Alpine, and Yuki Tsunoda of Racing Bulls.

“Huge congratulations to Kimi, an incredible result from him,” said Russell of Antonelli’s win.

“I knew he was going to be in the mix when I saw he was P5 and P4 on the leaderboard at the beginning… I was struggling on the tyres, but I’d have loved to be P1 today.”

The race started in dramatic fashion when Hamilton was forced off by teammate Leclerc.

The Monegasque, who is a two-time winner at Monza, then lost control on the exit of the Parabolica at the end of lap two, going straight into the gravel and flying side-on into the tyre barriers.

Leclerc stepped out of the car, looking winded but otherwise unhurt.

The race was red-flagged with Russell in the lead, having overtaken pole-sitter Pierre Gasly of Alpine.

Antonelli, who began at the back of the field in 19th after exceeding the permitted number of power-unit changes, had already moved his way up to 12th. Once the race restarted, he continued to pick his way through the field.

On lap 18, he hit the front for the first time, but that was the start of a desperate dogfight with Russell.

Antonelli benefited from a “free” tyre change during a virtual safety car on lap 29, coming out on a fresh set of mediums while Russell was left out on track with his hard tyres.

A 15-second lead quickly evaporated, and after a botched overtaking effort on lap 49, Antonelli finally slipped past Russell a lap later and eased his way through the final three laps to take the chequered flag.

articles.title: Arsenal come from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 and maintain perfect start
articles.summary: Gunners pass ⁠stiffest test so far in the defence of their Premier ⁠League title as they hit back after going behind.
articles.body:
Arsenal delivered an emphatic response to Chelsea’s emergence as potential Premier League title contenders with a 2-1 win that ended their rivals’ unbeaten start.

Mikel Arteta’s side trailed to a second-minute goal by Morgan Rogers in a pulsating London derby at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

But the champions showed why they are firm favourites to retain the title with a blistering response to that early setback.

Kai Havertz bagged the equaliser against his former club midway through the first half and Martin Odegaard netted Arsenal’s winner soon after the interval.

It was a statement of intent from second-placed Arsenal, who have won all three league matches to sit behind leaders Manchester City on goal scored.

The Gunners’ mature display underlined their desire to win the club’s first back-to-back titles since the 1930s.

For Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, the defeat ended his three-game winning run in all competitions since taking charge at Stamford Bridge in the close-season.

Alonso will realise just how much work Chelsea still have to do before they are in position to end a title drought dating back to 2017.

Chelsea’s shaky defence is prone to costly miscues, while their vaunted attack found it harder to flourish against Arsenal than in their free-scoring wins over Fulham, Luton and Brighton.

Arteta and Alonso have known each other since their days as childhood friends in the Basque region of Spain.

The chaotic matches of their youth on a gravel pitch in the Berio district of San Sebastian would have seemed calm in comparison to the blood and thunder their teams brought to a raucous corner of north London.

Chelsea beat Arsenal in the race to sign Rogers from Aston Villa in the close-season after the Gunners refused to match the Blues’ 117 million pound ($158m) bid for the England midfielder.

Rogers showed why Chelsea made him the most expensive British player in history as he put the Blues ahead after just 77 seconds.

Arsenal’s rock-solid defence had allowed just one shot on target in their first two games.

So often masters of the set-piece, Arteta’s men were found wanting at a free kick for once.

Reece James’ lofted delivery was not cleared by Declan Rice or Odegaard, giving Rogers the chance to drive a low volley past David Raya from the edge of the penalty area.

It was the first goal conceded by Arsenal this season.

Having conceded five times in their first two league games under Alonso, Chelsea’s three-man central defence remains flawed and they were exposed again in the 25th minute.

Havertz was allowed to drift from the right flank to the edge of the area unchecked by Jorrel Hato before the German smashed a low strike through the slow to react Maxence Lacroix’s legs and past Emiliano Martinez at his near post.

Martinez was signed from Villa to replace the error-prone Robert Sanchez but the Argentinian’s’s weak attempted save was hardly an improvement on his hapless predecessor.

Pedro Neto was inches away from restoring Chelsea’s lead just before half-time when the Portugal winger slapped his shot against the far post.

Where Chelsea were profligate, Arsenal have developed a ruthless touch in front of goal.

They exploited Chelsea’s weakness at the back to net with a superbly-crafted move in the 50th minute.

Christos Tzolis has made an impressive start following his close-season move from Club Brugge and the Greek winger’s incisive pass sliced through the Chelsea defence to Havertz.

The German’s clever dummy let the ball run through to Odegaard and he kept his composure to slot home from 10 yards.

Rogers’ angry clash with Rice prompted mocking chants of “you should have signed for a big club” from Arsenal fans.

Chelsea had chances to silence the taunts, but Malo Gusto blazed over from a good position before Estevao Willian’s rocket was tipped over by Raya in the final minutes.

Odegaard told Sky Sports it was a “massive” game for his side.

“It was a big, massive game, a tough opponent, really hard for us against a really good team,” he said.

“We always want to keep fighting and have shown that many times. Conceding early is never ideal, but our reaction was top – we could have scored some more goals and got our reward. I think it was a brilliant performance.”

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham gives Fever fans another chance to connect as meet & greet event gets new date
articles.summary: Indiana Fever fans will have another opportunity to connect with Sophie Cunningham after her live autograph signing received a new date. The event, organised...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever fans will have another opportunity to connect with Sophie Cunningham after her live autograph signing received a new date.

The event, organised by Prime Time Sports and Framing, will now take place on September 15 at noon ET after originally being scheduled for August 25.

The updated date is listed on the company's official eBay Live page, where Cunningham is the featured guest. Prime Time Sports also describes the event as a live-streamed private signing on their official website.

Sophie Cunningham event set for September 15

The rescheduled signing will give fans and collectors a chance to interact with Cunningham away from the basketball court.

Rather than watching the Fever forward compete in a WNBA game, supporters will be able to see her take part in a private signing while interacting with collectors and signing memorabilia.

Details regarding available items and participation can be found through Prime Time Sports and their eBay storefront.

The new date also comes before Indiana's return to action following the league's break for the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.

For Cunningham, the event provides an opportunity to spend time with the Fever supporters who have developed a strong connection with her.

Her aggressive style of play and willingness to defend her teammates have contributed to that bond, making the signing another chance for fans to connect with a player who has become a popular figure in Indiana.

The original August 25 date was postponed, meaning collectors will have to wait until September 15 for the event.

When the new date arrives, Cunningham will turn her attention away from the court for the signing before preparing for the Fever's return to WNBA action.

articles.title: Lakers predicted to part ways with Jaden Hardy to sign $63M veteran ex-Nuggets NBA champion
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are trying to get another name or two on the roster. It looks like if they want to, they are going to have to get rid of a recently ac...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have undergone plenty of roster turnover this season, officially ushering in the Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic era. The team made it to the second round of the playoffs before being swept by the Oklahoma City Thunder .

The Lakers are still looking to add to their roster, even though they are currently one player over the roster limit. As of late, they have been rumored to have a strong chance of landing NBA champion Bruce Brown.

"I think he's in the mix for the Lakers, a team that has had some interest in him for several years now," Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer said.

The challenge for Los Angeles is that multiple playoff-caliber teams are also in the mix for Brown. The veteran is an attractive free-agent option because of his ability to fill multiple roles and contribute in different ways.

"The Cavaliers , Heat and Lakers have recently expressed free agent interest in Bruce Brown. Now one of the best available unrestricted free agents, the versatile guard could help complete a title-contending rotation," NBA reporter Evan Sidery wrote.

The Lakers are going to have to move someone if they want to sign Brown to a deal. It is simply a matter of determining which player another team would be willing to take. Heavy.com's Sean Deveney believes Los Angeles would have to move Jaden Hardy.

"If the Lakers want to make a move that would free up room to add another player–Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer mentioned Bruce Brown as a possibility–they would probably need to make deals for both Knecht and Hardy, or offload a contract like that of Bronny James," Deveney wrote.

Hardy was brought to the Lakers this summer in exchange for Deandre Ayton, but it now looks like he could very well be on his way out. Brown getting to Los Angeles would be a significant addition, as his versatility could make him an ideal backup option behind Doncic or Reaves.

Brown has made $63 million throughout his career and brings plenty of valuable experience to the Lakers. Doncic and Reaves have both dealt with injuries at times, so having a veteran capable of stepping into the rotation when needed could be huge for LA.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel involving himself in Patriots’ star contract negotiations
articles.summary: Vrabel is doing his best to keep his roster intact.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are still trying to find a resolution to Christian Gonzalez's contract situation before the NFL season begins, and head coach Mike Vrabel is making it clear that he wants to help get a deal done.

However, Vrabel also understands that there is a line he cannot cross when it comes to negotiations between the Patriots and their star cornerback. With the regular season opener against the Seattle Seahawks just days away, the situation has become increasingly important for New England.

Vrabel wants to help resolve the situation

Aug 22, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel in the second quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Edward Finan-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Vrabel was asked Saturday whether he would give his input to the Patriots' front office or "go to bat" for Gonzalez during the contract negotiations.

The Patriots head coach acknowledged that he has been on both sides of these situations and wants to communicate with players the organization views as important to its future.

"I don't get involved in the negotiations, per se, but I certainly want to be involved in trying to get the situation resolved," Vrabel said .

That distinction is important. Vrabel isn't negotiating Gonzalez's contract himself, but he clearly wants to play a role in making sure the relationship between the player and organization remains strong.

Vrabel has also repeatedly emphasized how much he values Gonzalez as a player and how important he is to the Patriots.

Christian Gonzalez contract remains unresolved

Jan 25, 2026; Denver, CO, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reacts after an interception against the Denver Broncos in the 2026 AFC Championship Game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images

Gonzalez's contract situation has lingered throughout the offseason and preseason, and there is still no agreement with Week 1 approaching.

The 24-year-old cornerback is under contract, but he has not committed to playing in the Patriots' season opener against Seattle without a new extension. Gonzalez has described the situation as frustrating, while also remaining relatively tight-lipped about what he intends to do.

The Patriots reportedly have made an offer that would make Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history, but the two sides have yet to reach an agreement. Seattle's Devon Witherspoon recently reset the market with a four-year, $132 million extension, adding another important benchmark to the negotiations.

Dec 1, 2025; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) runs onto the field prior to the game against the New York Giants at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images

This is becoming more than just a contract story for New England.

The Patriots are preparing for a Super Bowl rematch against the Seahawks, and losing Gonzalez would be a significant blow to a defense that will have to deal with Seattle's explosive passing attack.

Vrabel has said he expects healthy players under contract to practice and play, but he also acknowledged that he has to prepare for every possible scenario.

For now, Vrabel is trying to stay focused on football while doing whatever he can to help resolve the Gonzalez situation. With the opener rapidly approaching, however, the pressure on the Patriots to get their star cornerback's future settled is only increasing.

articles.title: SEC power rankings shift after conference's dominant Week 1
articles.summary: The SEC is off to a perfect 15-0 start in 2026 with an average margin of victory over 39 points per game entering the Ole Miss versus Louisville game
articles.body:
The SEC is off to a dominant start in Week 1 of the 2026 college football season. Entering the Ole Miss -Louisville game, the SEC is a perfect 15-0 and the conference's average margin of victory is over 39 points per game.

The SEC did not get any scares against non-Power Four opponents in Week 1. The Georgia Bulldogs and the rest of the SEC teams that played non-Power Four foes all won by 17 points or more.

The LSU Tigers and Auburn Tigers both notched strong nonconference wins to start the season. LSU dominated Clemson 51-10 in coach Lane Kiffin's debut. The Tigers looked like SEC championship contenders and surged up a few spots to No. 3 in our power rankings.

Auburn earned a narrow win over the Baylor Bears , but did not have an impressive offensive performance. Still, Auburn is more proven than most of the conference for beating a Power Four opponent.
